scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new guest session. Initiate the POST /polEcoBoard/guests endpoint with valid IP address, device fingerprint, and initial consent status. Verify that a guest session record is created and a UUID is returned, and stored fields match the payload for analytics and compliance. Edge case: test with minimal required fields (e.g., IP address only, with device_fingerprint omitted) to validate optional schema. Ensure that privacy policy requirements are enforced, and that repeated calls from same IP/device combination are handled consistently.

Test failure scenario for guest session creation with invalid input. Attempt to create a guest session with improperly formatted IP address or missing required consent status in the payload. Verify the endpoint returns clear, actionable error messages indicating the specific business or validation failure. Ensure no guest session is actually created for invalid input.

Test successful soft deletion of a notification preference by an admin. First, register a new admin and log in to obtain privileges. Next, create a notification preference to have a target record. Then, call the DELETE /polEcoBoard/admin/notificationPreferences/{notificationPreferenceId} endpoint using the created ID and verify the response confirms successful deletion. Finally, confirm that a subsequent GET returns the deleted_at timestamp or that the item is not available in standard searches, ensuring compliance with retention and audit policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to gain 'admin' privileges required for this operation.
Login as admin to obtain a valid JWT for authenticating further API calls.
Create a new notification preference to be deleted in this test scenario.

scenarios.draft: Test paginated and filtered search for notification delivery failures as an authenticated member. Register and log in as a new member, ensure the member has at least one notification failure (via realistic prior failure or creation dependency), then call the search API with valid filters. Verify the results include only notification failures belonging to the authenticated member, with proper pagination metadata and security on cross-user visibility. Check the accuracy of key summary fields and that filtering/sorting works as intended.

dependencies.purpose: Create a test member account for authentication.
Obtain a valid token as a member.
Create at least one notification failure record (as admin) for use in test data, since members can't directly trigger real failures for testing.

scenarios.draft: Test search of all notification failures as a moderator, confirming access to all user failures (not just own) is permitted as per role. Register and log in a moderator, create failures for multiple users (members), and issue a PATCH request to /polEcoBoard/moderator/notificationFailures with a broad filter. Assert that multiple users' failures are visible and that fields not accessible to regular members are shown. Security must ensure no leakage to unauthorized members while providing full results to moderators. Also, test edge cases for filters by failure_code or provider.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as a moderator.
Obtain JWT for a moderator session.
Create at least one member account to simulate other users with notification failures.
Create notification failure records for multiple users as admin, enabling moderator visibility and filter tests.

scenarios.draft: Test full search and pagination of all notification failures as an admin. Register and log in as an admin, having several failure records for different members, including across multiple providers, codes, and delivery statuses. Submit a search request with advanced filters (failure_code, provider, status combinations) and verify the response contains failures across all users, full field visibility, correct sorting, and pagination controls for large result sets. Confirm security prevents access to non-admins/moderators. Also, check handling when filtering for non-existent codes or users (should return an empty result).

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as an admin user.
Acquire valid JWT as admin.
Create notification failure records for several different users and scenarios to ensure search realism.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a specific notification failure as a member. Register and log in as two different members. Create a notification failure for each. As member A, call GET on their own notificationFailureId and verify successful retrieval with complete details. Then, attempt to GET member B's notification failure as member A and confirm a permission error or not found is returned, demonstrating row-level security. Validate error responses and audit compliance for unauthorized access attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Register member A.
Log in as member A.
Register member B.
Log in as member B.
Create notification failure records for both member A and member B, referenced by their IDs.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of an anti-spam event record by an admin. First, register an admin and log in. Create a new anti-spam event via POST to obtain a valid antiSpamEventId. Then, update fields such as score, operation, or appeal status using this endpoint and verify that the record is correctly updated in the database. Ensure that business and audit constraints are enforced, and all changes are logged.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration to provide authorized access for updating anti-spam events.
Login as the registered admin to obtain credentials for authorized actions.
Create an anti-spam event entry and extract antiSpamEventId for the update test.

scenarios.draft: Test updating an anti-spam event with a non-existent antiSpamEventId. After admin authentication, attempt to update an event using a random or deleted UUID. Confirm the system returns a not-found error and does not corrupt the database. Verify that error messages are precise and audit logging occurs for failed operations.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for permissions.
Login to act with admin credentials.

scenarios.draft: Test hard deletion of an anti-spam event by an admin. Register and login as admin, create an anti-spam event, then delete it using this endpoint. Ensure that the event is permanently removed from the database and cannot be retrieved anymore. Confirm audit logs for compliance and that relationships or foreign keys do not cause issues on delete.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration to authorize deletion.
Login as admin to perform the action.
Create an anti-spam event to have a valid antiSpamEventId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to delete a non-existent anti-spam event by providing an invalid antiSpamEventId. System should return a not-found or similar error without affecting existing records. The test ensures business rules prevent deletion of non-existent records and that error messages are clear.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for proper authorization.
Login as admin to access the endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated list of consent status records with various filter criteria. Register as admin and login. Create several consent status log entries through POST. Then, use this PATCH endpoint to search by provider_key, consent_type, status, region, session id, and time window. Verify responses include only expected records, pagination works, and sensitive information is not leaked. Edge cases: filters with empty result, invalid filter syntax, and searching large datasets.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for permission to query consent statuses.
Login as admin to access protected resources.
Create multiple consent status records for search/filter tests.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a single consent status record by its unique ID. Register and login as admin. Create a consent status log, then fetch it with GET using its returned consentStatusId. Confirm that all expected fields (provider, status, region, audit context) are present, permissions are enforced, and non-admins are denied access.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for sufficient permissions.
Login as admin to use the GET endpoint.
Create a consent status record and obtain consentStatusId.

scenarios.draft: Test fetching a non-existent or already-deleted consent status record. After admin authentication, use a random or invalid consentStatusId in the GET request. Ensure system returns an appropriate error (not found), logs the attempt, and does not expose internal details.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for access.
Login as admin.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a user consent status by admin. Register and log in as admin. Use the POST endpoint with valid consent status input (provider_key, consent_type, region, status, session_anon_id, timestamps, audit context). Confirm the returned record is correctly stored, all compliance validations pass, and audit logs are created. Required fields must be present and business logic (such as uniqueness and schema validation) enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to gain write access for consent logs.
Login as the admin for authenticated requests.

scenarios.draft: Test rejection and error messaging for attempts to create a consent status with invalid, missing, or inconsistent input data (e.g., unsupported provider_key, missing region or consent_type, schema violation). The system should return detailed validation errors without creating the record, and ensure audit logging for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for endpoint access.
Login as admin before making invalid creation attempts.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator login workflow with both valid and invalid credentials. Start by registering a new moderator account (email, password, display name), ensuring registration succeeds. Attempt to login with correct credentials and validate that JWT tokens are issued and the moderator session is established. Then attempt login with incorrect password, unregistered email, and using an inactive or banned account (where possible), verifying the API returns appropriate errors for each. Assess rate limiting on repeated failed attempts and ensure security information is not leaked in error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new moderator account to allow login with valid credentials.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator logout operation, ensuring session tokens are invalidated and unauthorized API access is blocked after logout. Prerequisites include moderator registration and login to obtain JWT. Perform the logout call and ensure the API returns confirmation. Then attempt any protected moderator API with the same token to verify access is denied, confirming session revocation. Repeat with an already-logged-out token to check idempotency and proper error messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account which will be logged in.
Login as moderator to obtain valid JWT for the logout process.

scenarios.draft: Test the token validation logic for moderators. After registering and logging in as a moderator, use the provided JWT to call the validation endpoint and confirm that the token is accepted and the context is correct. Then test this endpoint with expired, revoked (after logout), and clearly malformed JWTs to verify invalid tokens produce correct unauthorized or error responses. Covers both success and various edge failure scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create coordinator to obtain a valid JWT via normal onboarding.
Obtain valid moderator JWT for subsequent validation tests.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator password change flow. Register and login as a moderator, then submit a valid password change request. After password is changed, verify all sessions are revoked and login is required. Attempt to change password with incorrect current password to validate error handling, and test weak/new password policy enforcement. Attempt protected API action with the old JWT after password change to ensure sessions are properly invalidated by this operation.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account for password change testing.
Login as moderator to obtain the current JWT token used in password change.

scenarios.draft: Test moderator token refresh by registering and logging in to obtain both access and refresh JWTs. Use the refresh token on this endpoint and confirm a new set of tokens is issued. Try using an already used (rotated out) or revoked refresh token to ensure the API returns an error and does not issue new tokens. Include testing of missing or malformed tokens in the request for correct failure handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account to enable the login/refresh process.
Obtain refresh and access tokens to test the refresh workflow.

scenarios.draft: Test member successful logout. Register a new member, log in to retrieve a valid authentication token, and use this token to log out. Confirm the session is revoked and that the token cannot be used for further authenticated actions (e.g., member validateToken).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to get credentials for login and session creation.
Login as the registered member to create an authentication session and retrieve JWT token.

scenarios.draft: Test member token validation for both success and failure cases. First, register and log in as a member to acquire a valid JWT token, then validate this token (should succeed). Next, after logout, re-validate the same token to confirm it is now invalid. Test validation with malformed or missing tokens to ensure proper error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to test authentication token flow.
Obtain a JWT token for validation.
Log out to simulate invalidated tokens and test validation failure after logout.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can successfully change their password and all sessions are revoked. Register and log in as a member, then change the password with the correct old password. After password change, confirm that previous tokens are no longer valid (validateToken should fail), and require a fresh login with the new password.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for the password change flow.
Obtain JWT token required to perform password change.

scenarios.draft: Test member password change failure due to incorrect current password. Attempt to change the password using an invalid existing password. The system should return a clear error with no change in account state. Authentication with both old and new passwords should reflect the proper status.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to initiate password change test.
Obtain JWT token for the password change attempt.

scenarios.draft: Test issuance of a new JWT via refresh token. Register and log in to obtain initial access and refresh tokens. Use the refresh token to request new tokens and ensure the refresh is successful. After prior logout or password change (which revokes sessions), attempt refresh again and confirm correct error code for revoked/invalid refresh token.

dependencies.purpose: Register member account for refresh workflow.
Log in to generate access and refresh tokens.
Optional: Verify that refresh token cannot be used once session is revoked.

scenarios.draft: Test successful registration of a new moderator. Provide unique email, valid password, display name, and required consent status. Validate that JWT tokens are issued upon registration and all moderator fields are populated. Follow up with moderator login using the registered credentials to confirm ability to authenticate and use moderator features.

dependencies.purpose: The scenario is for this endpoint; self-register and assert all fields and JWT returned.

This ensures uniqueness constraints are enforced for moderator emails.

Verify that all business and audit fields are correctly present, the audit trail includes proper reasoning and actor/admin information, and business rules prevent access if the audit does not exist or is not related to the specified moderationActionId. Also, verify that access is forbidden if a non-moderator attempts this operation.

dependencies.purpose: Register and obtain an authenticated moderator account for the test.

Create a moderation action record as the context for the audit.
Add an audit record to the moderation action to be fetched.

Attempt to create a moderation audit record with valid before/after state, rationale, and auditor/admin id. Verify response includes the new audit with all provided fields and proper audit context. Validate that the audit is immutable after creation, and only admins/moderators may perform this action.

dependencies.purpose: Set up an admin user and obtain authentication.
Authenticate admin for authorized calls.
Create a moderation action as the entity owning the moderation audit.

scenarios.draft: Test a moderator's ability to create a new moderation audit record linked to a moderation action. Authenticate as moderator, create a moderation action, then create an audit with all required business/log context. Confirm that the created record includes rationale, correct actor, pre/post state, and timestamps. Confirm error returned if fields missing or if performed by a non-moderator/non-admin.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a moderator account for the action.
Obtain appropriate moderator credentials.
Create the moderation action for which the audit is being added.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a moderation audit record's allowed fields (such as rationale or post-state) as an admin. Create admin and login, then create a moderation action and attached audit. Attempt to update metadata, rationale, or post-state for the given auditId, ensuring append-only or compliance restrictions are respected. Validate update is reflected, all changes are audit logged, and updates that violate immutable protocol (such as changing pre-state or auditId) are rejected. Test that non-admins and unauthorized users are denied update privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user.
Authenticate admin for update operations.
Create a moderation action as the parent record.
Create an audit record to update.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can update permitted fields (such as rationale or clarifying metadata) of a moderation audit record linked to a moderation action. Use moderator authentication, create the action, add the audit, then update fields per compliance rules. Assert that only modifiable fields are changed, updates are tracked in audit logs, and any attempt to modify immutable audit properties is rejected. Ensure update is not allowed for non-moderator/non-admin users.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for the test.
Login as moderator to receive auth token.
Create the moderation action entity for the test.
Create the initial audit record to be updated.

scenarios.draft: Test successful update of an operational log entry by an admin. Start by registering a new admin and logging in to obtain authorization. Create a new operational log entry to ensure a valid operationalLogId exists. Attempt to update allowed mutable fields (such as message or context) of this log with valid data. Verify the API returns the updated record reflecting the new details, and that immutable fields remain unchanged. Ensure all changes are correctly tracked for compliance and audit.

dependencies.purpose: Obtain an admin role account and receive authorization headers for privileged access.
Authenticate as admin and get active JWT to use in the update operation.
Create a new operational log entry and get operationalLogId to be used in update tests.

scenarios.draft: Test failure when attempting to update an immutable field (such as log_level, timestamp, or primary key) in an operational log as admin. After registering and logging in as admin and creating a log entry, send an update request attempting to modify immutable fields. Confirm that the API rejects the update, returns an appropriate error message, and does not alter the record.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account for authentication and authorization.
Authenticate and obtain JWT tokens to authorize the operation.
Create an operational log entry to update and test immutable field validation.

scenarios.draft: Test successful soft deletion of an operational log record by an admin user. Begin by registering and logging in as an admin, then create a new operational log entry. Issue a DELETE request for the created operationalLogId and verify that the deleted_at timestamp is set, the log is no longer visible to standard queries, and that all necessary compliance/audit logs are updated. Also check that attempts to fetch the log by ID after deletion reflect its deleted state or result in a not-found error, depending on business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for authorization.
Log in as the admin user and get authorization headers.
Insert an operational log to have a valid operationalLogId for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and paging through audit trail records as an admin. After registering and logging in as admin and creating several audit trail records, submit a PATCH request with various filter and pagination parameters, such as actor, action type, date range, or resource filters. Confirm that the returned records match the search criteria, correct pagination metadata is provided, and that all sensitive or role-specific information is handled as per access policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for performing privileged operations.
Authenticate and authorize as admin.
Insert audit trail records to have data for search and pagination testing.

scenarios.draft: Test successfully retrieving a single audit trail record by auditTrailId as an admin. Register and login as admin, create a new audit trail, then request its details using the correct ID. Check that the full compliance and change details are present and that access control is properly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Make an admin account for authentication.
Get admin authentication for subsequent requests.
Create an audit trail record to retrieve.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when retrieving an audit trail record with a non-existent or already-deleted auditTrailId as admin. Register and login as admin, then issue a GET request with an ID that does not exist in the system. Validate that the API responds with a clear not-found error message and does not leak sensitive data.

dependencies.purpose: Generate admin account for privileged access.
Log in for authorization context.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new immutable audit trail entry as admin. Start by registering and logging in as an admin. Attempt to create an audit trail with valid action type, actor, target resource, context, and timestamp. Verify that the audit trail is persisted, immutable, and the response contains the full context as specified.

dependencies.purpose: Establish an admin user for authenticated operations.
Log in as admin to authorize the audit trail creation.

Ensure results are restricted to admin role, only non-deleted providers are shown by default, but advanced filters can include disabled or deleted providers if specified. Validate correct pagination metadata and that search on provider name, status, and jurisdiction returns relevant results. Edge case: searching with filters that yield zero results. Attempt unauthorized access by non-admin to confirm permission enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for authentication context. This must be performed first.

Create external auth providers for use in search/filter tests.

Validate all provider fields are returned as described, including identity, operational status, jurisdiction, privacy and compliance fields, and that no PII is leaked. Edge cases: querying a nonexistent externalAuthProviderId returns not-found error; soft-deleted provider returns appropriate status. Attempt unauthorized access with non-admin role to verify access control.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to perform authenticated queries.
Obtain a valid admin auth token.

Attempt to create another provider with the same provider_key or name and validate duplicate error is returned. Edge cases: supply invalid status value or malformed URI and confirm validation error. Attempt unauthenticated provider creation to ensure access is denied for non-admins.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin with permission to add external auth providers.
Log in as admin to get authorization for provider creation.

scenarios.draft: Test update of an external authentication provider by admin: valid changes to status (enabled/disabled/maintenance), jurisdiction info, URIs, description, and compliance fields. Ensure uniqueness constraints apply for key fields (e.g., cannot set provider_key to collide with existing). Try to update an already soft-deleted provider and confirm failure. Confirm audit logging is performed and updated fields are reflected in the result. Attempt update by non-admin and verify permission denied.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can soft-delete an external authentication provider by ID. Confirm attempts to use/re-fetch the provider for operational tasks reflect a deleted state. Ensure audit/tracking of delete action, deletion is blocked if there are dependent business constraints (if applicable), and non-admins cannot perform delete. Check deletion of a non-existent or already deleted provider returns correct errors.

Validate that a member receives successful registration, is_active is set to true, and no password hash is returned. Then, attempt to register another account with the same email and expect a duplicate email error, verifying uniqueness enforcement and precise error messaging.

Test member registration fails with invalid email format and with a password that does not meet complexity requirements. Ensure meaningful error responses are returned for each violation and the account is not created.

Test admin updating a member's profile, including fields such as display name and profile image URI. A successful update returns the updated member with all changes. Then, attempt to update the display name to one already used by another member, verifying that the API rejects the change due to uniqueness constraints, returning a detailed error message.

scenarios.draft: Test soft-deletion (deactivation) of a member account as an admin. The member record should be marked as deleted (deleted_at) and must appear inactive on the platform, but retain audit information. Attempt to soft-delete the same member a second time and verify that the API returns an error indicating the member is already deleted or inactive, ensuring appropriate business rule enforcement.

scenarios.draft: Test admin search for moderators with filtering (by appointment date, status, or privilege), checking that only admin role can use this endpoint. Validate both successful filter results and the behavior when no moderators match the filters (empty result set, with correct pagination metadata). Attempt access with insufficient privileges (non-admin), ensuring access is denied with a permission error message.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for authorized moderator search.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve full details of an existing moderator account by moderatorId, confirming that all visible properties (status, member association, appointer admin, etc.) are present. Attempt to retrieve a moderator that does not exist, ensuring the API returns a not-found error, and attempt with unauthorized (non-admin) credentials to verify permission enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for privilege to access moderator details.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to delete a notification provider using a non-existent or invalid notificationProviderId. The endpoint should return a not found or similar error; no prior provider creation is necessary. Ensure business logic protects against deletion of non-existing records.

scenarios.draft: Test searching operational logs with minimal filters to retrieve recent operational activities as an admin. Register and login as admin. Ensure the resulting log list contains expected records, paginates correctly, and returns all mandatory summary fields. Validate that filtering, pagination, and sorting operate as specified for the endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin to use the search endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieving the details of a specific operational log by operationalLogId. Register and authenticate as admin, then create a new operational log entry to obtain the ID. Perform the GET operation and verify that all expected fields (log level, message, event code, context, timestamp, actor, etc.) are returned accurately and match the created log data.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin.
Create an operational log entry to obtain a valid operationalLogId for retrieval.

scenarios.draft: Test attempting to retrieve an operational log with a non-existent or already-deleted operationalLogId as admin. Confirm the system returns a clear error indicating record not found. This validates proper error handling for fetch and compliance access.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to access the endpoint.

scenarios.draft: Test successful creation of a new operational log by an admin. Begin by registering and logging in as admin. Call the POST endpoint with required fields (log level, message, event code, metadata). Verify that the response contains the expected log entry with all supplied data and generated metadata (timestamp, actor).

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin to perform creation of an operational log.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully soft-delete a board history event by its unique boardHistoryId. First, register a new admin and moderator via their registration endpoints, and login both users. Then, the admin creates a category and board, and assigns the moderator to the board. The moderator creates a board history event, then performs a DELETE using the event's boardHistoryId. Confirm that the board history's deleted_at is set, and that it no longer appears in standard queries, but remains accessible for audit. All steps must follow correct permission roles.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin; this is needed for all board category, board, and assignment creation.
Log the admin in to obtain credentials for protected endpoints.
Admin creates a category as a prerequisite for board creation.
Admin creates a board associated with the category, needed for moderator assignment and board history actions.
Moderator registration to perform moderator-only actions.
Moderator login to obtain required privileges for the test.
Admin assigns the moderator to the created board.
Moderator creates a board history event for the board.

scenarios.draft: Test admin ability to soft-delete a board history event by its boardHistoryId. Flow: register and login as admin, create a category and board, create a board history event for the board, then issue DELETE on boardHistoryId as admin. Verify the board history is no longer available in standard queries and its deleted_at timestamp is set. Confirm actions are logged and audit/history is audit-accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to perform the required admin tasks in the test.
Login the new admin in order to perform privileged operations.
Create a category for the new board that will have board histories.
Create a board under the new category for board history creation.
Create a board history entry for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can search for their assigned boards using filters and pagination. The test covers success and edge cases: first, register and login as moderator and admin, create a category, a board, and assign the moderator to the board. Have the moderator query assignments with filters for moderatorId, boardId, and status, verifying that only matching assignments are returned. Test pagination and search with no results when filters do not match any assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator to perform search as a logged-in moderator.
Login as moderator to search assignments.
Register a new admin for privileged actions (board setup, assignment).
Admin login for creating board/category and assigning moderator.
Admin creates a category for a new board.
Admin creates a board, required for making assignments.
Admin assigns the moderator to the new board.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can search and filter all moderator-board assignments using multiple criteria and pagination. Register and login as admin, create two moderators via their respective flows, create a category and two boards, assign each moderator to a board, and use PATCH with advanced filtering to search assignments by moderatorId, boardId, adminId, status, and pagination. Test both successful and empty result scenarios for complex, multi-criteria searches.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for all assignment/board actions.
Admin login for privileged task flows.
Create category to allow board instantiation.
Create boards for assignment events.
Create first moderator for assignment.
Login as first moderator for mod id reference.
Create second moderator for assignment.

Assign second moderator to another board.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of a moderator-board assignment by ID as a logged-in moderator. After registering and logging in both moderator and admin, the admin creates a category, a board, assigns the moderator, and returns the assignmentId. The moderator retrieves the assignment by {moderatorBoardAssignmentId}, expecting assignment details for a valid ID. Then, attempt to fetch with a random/non-existent assignmentId and confirm a not found/forbidden error is returned. Also, ensure moderators only see assignments they are authorized to view.

dependencies.purpose: Moderator sign-up for authorization.
Moderator login to perform get by ID.
Admin registration to perform pre-requisite steps.
Login as admin to create board and make assignments.
Create category for new board.
Board creation for use in assignment.
Assign moderator to board, generating an assignmentId.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully retrieve full details of a specific vote on a comment. Steps: (1) Register a moderator, login to obtain moderator token. (2) Register a member, login as member, create a post and add a comment. (3) Have the member cast a vote on the comment. (4) As moderator, fetch the vote details using commentId and voteId. Verify all fields (vote value, voter, timestamp, referential integrity) are returned. Confirm the moderator only accesses records they are permitted to view. Also check permission error if a non-moderator attempts access.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for authorization to fetch vote details using moderator-level endpoint.
Login as moderator to obtain valid JWT authorization token for request.
Register a basic member for content creation and voting tests.
Login as member to create a post and comment.
Create a post as member, providing a context for comment creation.
Create a comment on the post to be voted on by the member.
Member votes on the comment, creating the vote to be queried by the moderator.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin user can retrieve all information for a specific vote on a comment. Steps: (1) Register and login as admin. (2) Register a member, login as member, create a post and comment. (3) Let the member vote on the comment. (4) As admin, fetch vote details using commentId/voteId. Verify admin receives full, correct information. Also attempt access with insufficient privileges (e.g., as guest or other member) and verify forbidden access with proper error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for privileged vote inspection.
Login as admin user to access the required endpoint.
Register another member account to simulate regular user actions.
Login as member to allow creation of post and comment.
Create a post to provide context for the comment and votes.
Create a comment under the post to allow voting.
Add a vote so there is a voteId to retrieve as admin.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can successfully upvote/downvote a comment and that business rules prevent multiple votes from the same member on the same comment. Steps: (1) Register and login as a member. (2) Create a post, add a comment. (3) Cast a vote (upvote or downvote) as permitted. (4) Attempt to cast a second vote as the same member on the same comment. Verify that the first attempt succeeds and the second results in a business error for duplicate voting. Additionally, ensure that voting on own comment or when banned is not allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Register member who will vote on comments.
Login as member to obtain access.
Create a post for the comment thread context.
Create a target comment to vote on.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can update their own vote on a comment (changing from upvote to downvote, or vice versa) within the allowed business rule update window. Steps: (1) Register and login as member. (2) Create post, create comment, cast initial vote. (3) Update the vote using voteId and commentId, and verify the change is reflected in the database and audit trail. (4) Attempt update after update window expiration (if enforced by business rules) or by another member, expecting error response for not authorized or update period ended.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for vote placement and update.
Login for authorized actions.
Create the post which will host the comment.
Create a comment to allow voting.
Cast the initial vote needed for update testing.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can delete (retract) their own vote from a comment and that deletion adheres to business policy (e.g., within voting window, not allowed by non-owner). Steps: (1) Register and login as member. (2) Create a post, comment, and cast a vote. (3) Delete the vote and confirm it is removed from tallies and is not queryable. (4) Attempt deletion by another member (not vote owner) and confirm error for forbidden action. (5) Optionally, attempt to delete after allowed period and confirm appropriate error policy or no effect.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will create and later delete a vote.
Login for vote/deletion permissions.
Create post for vote activity context.
Create comment to vote on.
Place initial vote for deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Test successful retrieval of complete details for a specific moderation action as a moderator. Scenario requires a moderator account with proper authentication. First, create the required entities such as a reportable post or comment, trigger a moderation action (e.g., remove, warn, escalate) as a moderator, and then use the moderationActionId to fetch and verify that all audit-trail fields, rationale, operator info, and relevant metadata are correctly returned for the moderation action. Ensure that fields match the business logic and that full details are returned for the logged-in moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Register and onboard a new moderator with a unique email, display name, and consent. Required for authenticated access to moderation endpoints.
Login as the moderator to obtain authentication tokens for protected API actions.
Trigger a new moderation action (e.g., removal or warning) to supply a valid moderationActionId for the detail lookup in this test.

scenarios.draft: Test error handling when a moderator attempts to retrieve details for a moderation action that does not exist. Use a valid moderator authentication context and supply a random or previously deleted moderationActionId, then verify that the API returns a clear not-found or error status as defined in the business rules. Ensure the error message is descriptive and does not expose sensitive business internals.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for authenticated access.
Login to obtain tokens for the test.

scenarios.draft: Test admin ability to retrieve all business and audit metadata for a specific moderation action. First, register and log in as an admin, create a moderation action via appropriate logic (e.g., issue warning, remove content through a report flow), and then fetch its details using the moderationActionId. Validate that all fields relevant to compliance and audit are returned and follow business policy for admin context.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for privileged API access.
Login as admin to receive authentication tokens.
Create a moderation action as admin to use its ID in the retrieval test.

scenarios.draft: Test error scenario when an unauthenticated or insufficiently privileged user attempts to fetch detailed moderation action information via the admin endpoint. Verify that access is denied and the system returns a relevant error message indicating lack of authorization or privilege. Confirm no private or sensitive information is disclosed in error responses.

Test creation of a new moderation action (e.g., removal, warning, edit, or escalation) as an authenticated moderator. This requires having a reportable entity (such as a post or comment), followed by submission of all required fields in business logic—report reference, operator ID, action type, rationale, and status. Ensure the system records the new moderation action, returns all audit metadata, and that related audit logs are produced. Check that only valid business logic-compliant actions can be created, and no sensitive fields are omitted.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator required for authentication.
Login as moderator for API access.

scenarios.draft: Test scenario where creation of a moderation action with invalid or missing required fields is attempted. Supply an incomplete or malformed request as a moderator, and verify that the system rejects the operation with clear, actionable validation errors (such as missing action type, invalid target, or incomplete rationale) and does not create the moderation action.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator account for authentication.
Login as moderator for API context.

scenarios.draft: Test creation of a new moderation action by an admin. Authenticate as admin, provide valid action context (target post/comment), specify all required business fields, and verify successful creation with proper audit-log return values. Ensure role-based creation (admin) is respected and that the created action can immediately be fetched for audit and downstream workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for privileged testing.
Login to admin for authorization.

scenarios.draft: Attempt to create a moderation action as admin but omit required fields (e.g., rationale, action type). The API should respond with validation errors and not persist the action. Validate error message clarity and check that audit logs reflect the failed attempt as intended by compliance requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for authenticated access.
Log in to obtain authentication.

scenarios.draft: Test updating the status, rationale, or correctable fields of an existing moderation action as an authenticated moderator. First, create a reportable post/comment, initiate a moderation action, and then update the moderationActionId with modified fields (e.g., changing rationale or status). Confirm that changes are applied only to allowed fields, audit logs are updated, and business state reflects updated action.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator required for test workflow.
Login as moderator for workflow.
Create a moderation action to have a modifiable moderationActionId.

scenarios.draft: Test scenario where a moderator attempts to update a moderation action that either does not exist or has become immutable (locked/finalized by business rules). Verify that the update is rejected with a clear error message about invalid or unauthorized mutation and confirm that no unintended changes are made to system state.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator to access API.
Login as moderator for workflow.

scenarios.draft: As an admin, retrieve detailed information about a specific report filed for a post. First, register an admin account and login to obtain the necessary permissions. Then, create a member, create a post as the member, and submit a report for the post. Finally, retrieve the report by its reportId and postId, and verify that the full report details are returned. This scenario confirms successful fetch for authorized admin with valid identifiers.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account and obtain authorization tokens for subsequent admin-level actions.
Login as the admin to receive authentication tokens.
Register a standard member to perform member actions such as post and report creation.
Login as member to create a post and report for test setup.
Member creates a post which will later be reported, ensuring valid postId for the report.
Member submits a report on the created post to generate a reportId.

scenarios.draft: Test edge cases where admin tries fetching a report using invalid or non-existent postId or reportId, or with insufficient permissions. Start by registering an admin and ensuring valid login. Attempt to retrieve a report using malformed or random UUIDs for postId/reportId, and verify that appropriate 'not found', 'forbidden', or error messages are returned. This test ensures robust error handling for bad input or unauthorized access.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for test actions.
Login as admin to get tokens for admin requests.

scenarios.draft: As a member, submit a report about a post. Validate that reporting is only allowed for authenticated members and that duplicate reports by the same member for the same post are prevented. The scenario proceeds as follows: First, register and login as a member. Create a post as another member account to ensure the reporting member is not the author, then submit a report (reason code and description) for the post. Verify that the report is created. Try to submit a second report as the same member for the same post and confirm the API returns a duplicate error. This tests report creation flow and de-duplication logic.

scenarios.draft: Test post report submission fails for unauthenticated users and for invalid reason codes. Attempt to report a post without authentication and confirm a 401 or forbidden error occurs. Then, while authenticated, try submitting reports with invalid or missing reason codes/descriptions to cause schema validation errors, confirming proper error messaging and enforcement.

scenarios.draft: As a moderator, attempt to submit a report for a specific post. First, register and login as a moderator to obtain authorization. Create a post as a different member. Use moderator credentials to submit a new report for that post, providing reason and description. Validate that moderator-originated reports are accepted and that duplicate moderation reports for the same post are handled according to business rules. This tests both privilege-based access and normal reporting logic from a moderator role perspective.

scenarios.draft: Check moderator role attempting to submit a report with incomplete or invalid fields (e.g., missing reason, reporting own post). Attempt to report a post authored by the same moderator, or submit with missing data, and verify that validation errors or business rule errors are returned as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator, who will create a post and then attempt to report it as self.
Login as moderator for all steps.
Moderator creates a post and then attempts to report it.

scenarios.draft: As an admin, attempt to submit a new report for a post. Register as admin, login, and create a post via a member account. Submit a report for that post as the admin. Confirm the report is properly created and that all required fields are enforced. Attempt to submit another report for same post as the same admin and verify duplicate prevention is active. Also test with missing required fields or invalid post to verify business logic and error responses.

scenarios.draft: As a moderator, update an existing post report by adding moderation notes, adjusting reason code, or resolving the report. Register and login as a moderator, ensure there is a valid post and a report created for it (by a member), then as moderator update the report using the reportId and postId combination. Confirm all permitted fields are updatable, and that audit trails are preserved. Test both valid updates and forbidden attempts (such as a moderator attempting to update a report without proper permissions or for a non-existent report) to verify access control and robust error handling.

Register member who will create a post and report.
Login as member to set up the post and file the initial report.
Member creates a post which will later be reported.
Member files a report on a post to generate reportId for moderation.

scenarios.draft: Verify that an admin can fetch the full editable and audit history for a specific post. Prerequisites include registering an admin account, logging in to obtain authorization, creating a member post, and generating several post edits (edits recorded in history). Scenario should ensure correct filtering and pagination behavior, return of all allowed audit metadata, and testing against a post with a rich history of edits. Includes checking empty result for posts with no edits and access denial if admin is unauthorized or improperly authenticated.

Create the original post to be used as the subject for edit history.
Generate one or more post edits to populate the edit history for the post. This must be performed after post creation and by an authorized user (the author, moderator, or admin).

scenarios.draft: Validate that a post's author (member) can fetch the full detail of a single edit made to their post. Steps: member registration, login, post creation, post edit creation, then querying the postEditId as the member. Should ensure all historical edit content, rationale, actor, and timestamp fields are present, and that access control restricts viewing solely to permitted actors (author, moderator, admin).

Steps: register post author, register a second member, create post/edit as first member, then attempt to access post edit detail as the second member.

Process: register a moderator, login as moderator, produce a member post and edit, then use the moderator endpoint to retrieve the edit detail and confirm full data access including actor, content, reason, and timestamps. Should validate permission enforcement and prohibit access to non-existent edit IDs.

scenarios.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve complete details for any post edit, regardless of author or moderator, confirming full permission. Scenario: create an admin, login, produce a member post and post edit, then retrieve postEditId detail as admin to confirm access. Should also validate error response for non-existent or deleted postEditId.

Create the post for editing and history.
Produce one or more edits for the post so that the admin has something to review.

scenarios.draft: Ensure a member can create an edit record for a post they authored. Steps: member registration, login, post creation, post edit operation. Validate correct audit, editor ID match, and that the new edit is visible in post edit history. Also cover that creating multiple edits correctly appends history entries and increments version/revision counters where relevant.

Author creates a post for subsequent editing.

scenarios.draft: Verify a member cannot create an edit record for a post they do not own (permission denied scenario). Steps: two separate member accounts, first creates post, second attempts to create an edit for the other's post - should return forbidden error for second member.

scenarios.draft: Test updating a specific incident record by its unique ID as an admin. First, register an admin account and log in to acquire the necessary authorization. Create a new incident record to obtain a valid incidentId. Attempt a successful update by changing the description or status (e.g., set it to 'resolved') and verify the changes persist in the system. Also, attempt to update immutable properties such as the incident code or creation timestamp to verify that such operations are correctly rejected with validation errors. Additionally, check that only admins are permitted to perform updates, and attempts by other roles or unauthenticated users result in appropriate permission errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to acquire admin-level system access required to update an incident.
Log in as admin to acquire a valid JWT token for authorization.

scenarios.draft: Test hard deletion of an incident record by its unique incidentId as a super-admin. Begin by registering and logging in as an admin. Create an incident to ensure there is at least one incident record to delete. Attempt to delete the incident and verify it is removed from the list of incidents. Check that all related compliance, auditing, and reporting rules are enforced (e.g., mandatory logging of deletion with rationale). Test error responses for attempts to delete non-existent, already deleted, or unauthorized record deletions; ensure such attempts yield clear error messages. Validate that only an admin can perform this deletion operation and that other user types receive a permission denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a super-admin/admin user to perform the incident deletion operation.

Create a new incident entry, providing a valid incidentId for the deletion test.

scenarios.draft: Test searching and retrieving maintenance window events using filtering, sorting, and pagination as an admin. Register and log in as an admin first. Create multiple maintenance window records with varying codes, impact types, and time windows. Perform a search query without filters, then with specific filters such as time range, status, and code to verify correct results. Validate the pagination and sorting behaviors. Also, test edge cases such as invalid filter syntax, empty results, and permission denial for unauthenticated users.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to ensure appropriate permissions to search maintenance windows.

Create a new maintenance window and use its ID to fetch the record with the GET method, ensuring the returned details match exactly what was stored. Attempt retrieval of a non-existent or deleted maintenanceWindowId and confirm the system returns a not-found error. Finally, confirm access is restricted to admins and unauthorized requests are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for authorized access.
Log in as admin to gain authorization.
Create a new maintenance window to provide a valid maintenanceWindowId for the GET test.

scenarios.draft: Test creating a new maintenance window via admin endpoint. Register and log in as an admin to obtain authorization. Submit valid creation data and verify the maintenance window is correctly stored with all specified details. Attempt to create another maintenance window with conflicting or invalid input (such as overlapping windows or invalid time range) and check that the API returns the expected validation errors. Also, confirm that only admins can perform creation and unauthenticated or unauthorized requests are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin as prerequisite for maintenance window creation.
Log in as admin to obtain the JWT required for authorized creation requests.

Create one or more boards (requires an admin to create categories and boards), perform board changes to generate board history records (such as moving a board to a different category or editing board metadata through the admin). Then, as an authenticated moderator, perform a PATCH request to fetch board history using various filters (by change type, actor, time range, board, category, etc.) and verify: (1) Board history returns only events moderator has access to; (2) Filters, sorting, and pagination operate as expected; (3) Edge cases such as no results, invalid filters, or forbidden access are handled with proper errors; (4) Audit compliance and operational constraints are present.

Create discussion boards linked to categories, so history records can exist.

Register and log in as admin, ensure several board changes to establish a meaningful audit log. Use a PATCH request to /polEcoBoard/admin/boardHistories with a variety of filters (change_type, actor, board, category, date interval), confirming: (1) Admin can view all relevant history entries; (2) Filtering and pagination work as specified; (3) Access is denied for unauthorized roles; (4) Robust input validation and error messaging for improper filter parameters or missing context.

Expect: (1) Moderator receives all permitted details and references (board, categories, actor, rationale); (2) Invalid or unauthorized history IDs return not found or permission error; (3) Edge case of non-existent or deleted IDs handled correctly; (4) Permission matrix is enforced – moderator only sees records according to business rules.

scenarios.draft: Test the ability for a moderator to soft-delete (archive) a board status record. Register and log in as a moderator, ensure a valid board and an associated status event exist (admin must create category and board, then a moderator status event is created). As the moderator, delete the existing board status event by its ID and verify: (1) The event is marked deleted (deleted_at set); (2) Deleted event is no longer visible in active listings but retained for audit; (3) Attempts to delete non-existent, already-deleted, or unauthorized IDs return correct error responses; (4) Proper compliance logging is performed for moderation action.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for test authentication.
Moderator login for secure operations.
Admin registration for board/category creation.
Admin login for setup.
Create a category as the context for board.
Create board linked to category.
Moderator creates a board status event to set up for deletion.

Register and log in as admin, ensure a board and a relevant status exist (by creating category, board, and a board status event via another admin or moderator). Then perform a DELETE on /polEcoBoard/admin/boardStatuses/{boardStatusId} to archive the status event. Validate: (1) Event is flagged with deleted_at, not physically deleted; (2) It becomes inaccessible from active board status queries; (3) Audit trail logs are updated for compliance; (4) Edge cases such as attempting to delete already-deleted or non-existent status IDs are handled safely with business-meaningful errors; (5) Action is denied for users without admin role.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for authentication context.
Admin login to establish permissions.
Create a category as prerequisite for boards.
Create discussion board used in status event.
Create a board status event as admin or by assigning a moderator, so that a status event exists for deletion.

scenarios.draft: Test that a moderator can search and retrieve escalation records filtered by various attributes, such as status, actor, rationale, and date range. Verify that only escalations visible to the moderator (based on their role and board assignments) are returned. Ensure pagination and sorting work as intended. Test for no-result scenarios and input validation errors (e.g., invalid filter fields). Attempting to search with insufficient privileges should result in a permission error. scenarios.draft: Test the successful soft-deletion of a comment on a post by an admin. First, create a member who makes a post and a comment on that post. Register and log in as an admin. The admin deletes the member's comment using this endpoint and verifies that the comment is no longer visible in general post comments listing but remains visible to admin for audit. Also, test deletion of a comment as an admin when the comment has already been deleted, expecting validation error or idempotence. Additionally, verify that attempting to delete a comment on a non-existent or already deleted post or with an invalid commentId results in an appropriate error message. Permission checks must ensure that only admins can successfully use this endpoint; attempts by non-admins must be denied with a permission error.

scenarios.draft: Test that a member can successfully retrieve the edit history for their own comment using this endpoint. Create a post and a comment, then perform multiple edits to the comment. Use the endpoint to fetch the list of edit history records, verifying all revisions are returned, including body, editor, timestamp, and rationale. Also test filtering and pagination options in the request—e.g., restricting by date or limiting number of history records per request. Validation must ensure an empty history (when no edits are present) is handled gracefully. Attempts to query edit history of a non-existent comment or as a member who does not own the comment should be denied or gracefully error out, according to business rules. Attempting to access another user's comment edit history must return a permission error or an empty result for privacy.

scenarios.draft: Test retrieval of comment edit history as a moderator, including audit and compliance use cases. Register a member to create a post and comment, then perform edits to generate a history. Register and login as a moderator. Use the endpoint to fetch the full revision trail of that comment as a moderator, verify access to all edit history even if the moderator is not the original author. Test advanced filtering by editor_member_id or date range. Also, confirm that attempts to request edit history for invalid or non-existent comments, as well as insufficient permissions (non-moderators), return proper error responses. Ensure that the moderator can access edit history for comments by any member for governance purposes, in line with role-based access rules. Verify empty result and edge cases are handled gracefully.

Use this endpoint as the admin to get the full revision list for the comment, confirming that all edit events are visible, regardless of ownership, and audit information is complete (editor, reason, timestamp). Validate search/filter and pagination parameters work as expected. Edge cases include requesting edit history for non-existent comments or posts, and ensuring correct error messages are returned. Permission validation: test an unauthenticated user or a user with insufficient privileges cannot access this data. Confirm empty edit histories are handled without error.

scenarios.draft: Test that the member who authored a comment can fetch detailed information about a single comment edit using its edit ID. Retrieve a specific edit via this endpoint and verify the returned information (body at edit time, editor ID, reason, timestamp) is correct and matches edit history. Additionally, attempt to fetch edit details for a comment the member does not own, expecting a permission or privacy error. Fetching a non-existent or invalid edit ID should result in a 'not found' or validation error. Ensure privacy boundaries and business rules are enforced to only allow authorized access to edit details, and error messages are descriptive for auditability.
