Register a moderator to enable detail lookup by moderatorId.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to create a notification preference with the same event type and channel for the same moderator results in an error due to duplication. First, a moderator registers and logs in. Then, the moderator creates a notification preference specifying an event type and channel. Finally, the moderator attempts to create another notification preference with the identical event type and channel, expecting the system to return an error indicating that a duplicate preference is not allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new moderator account to provide the required authorization context.
Log in as the created moderator to obtain JWT for subsequent authorized requests.
Create the initial notification preference as a prerequisite for testing duplicate creation logic.

scenario.draft: Test the successful creation of a notification preference as an admin and check enforcement of event type/channel constraints. Begin by registering a new admin account and logging in. Use valid and supported event types and channels for the request. The created record should be returned with accurate audit/compliance fields. Then, attempt to create a notification preference using an unsupported or invalid event or channel. The API should respond with a clear error message specifying invalid value or unsupported field.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin account to receive admin-level authorization.
Log in to obtain JWT Authorization required for admin-only endpoints.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can update their own notification preference by ID, modifying the opt-in/out status or channel. First, register and log in as a member. Create a notification preference. Then, update the created notification preference, changing status or channel. Validate that the change is reflected in the updated record. This confirms members can update their own preferences as described in business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member account for testing self-service notification preferences.
Log in to the created member account.
Create a new notification preference for the logged-in member to serve as the object for the update scenario.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a member cannot update another user's notification preference. Register Member A and Member B separately. Member A creates a notification preference. Attempt to update Member A's notification preference using Member B's credentials. The API should return a permission denied error, validating enforcement of self-ownership on preference changes.

dependencies.purpose: Register two member accounts (Member A and Member B).
Login as Member A to create the notification preference, then login as Member B to attempt unauthorized update.
Create a notification preference using Member A's session.

scenario.draft: Test admin's ability to update notification preferences for any user. First, register an admin and a member, both logged in. The member creates a notification preference. The admin then updates the member's notification preference. The successful update should be reflected in the returned record. This covers full-lifecycle admin compliance and recourse scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to perform administrative update.
Login as admin to obtain JWT credentials.
Register a member who will own the notification preference.
Login as member to create the initial notification preference as the update target.
Create the notification preference as the member, so it can be updated by the admin.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can soft-delete their own notification preference record by ID. Register a member, log in, and create a notification preference. Then, perform a soft delete. Confirm the deleted_at timestamp is set and the record is excluded from routine searches. This scenario verifies self-deletion compliance and audit retention.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to be the owner of the notification preference.
Login as the member to perform preference operations.
Create a notification preference to serve as the delete target.

scenario.draft: Ensure a member cannot delete another user's notification preference. Register Member A and Member B. Member A creates a notification preference. Member B attempts to delete Member A's preference and is denied. This validates proper permissions and self-scoped deletion enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register Member A and Member B accounts.
Login as Member A to create the preference, then as Member B to attempt the unauthorized delete.
Member A creates the target preference record.

scenario.draft: Test a successful update of an existing notification provider's configuration by an admin. Begin by registering a new admin account and logging in to obtain admin privileges. Next, create a new notification provider using the appropriate endpoint, acquiring the notificationProviderId for update. Finally, execute the PUT operation to update mutable information such as the provider's name, supported channels, endpoint URI, or status. Assert that the returned record reflects the updated values, and that immutable fields (such as provider_key) remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register and obtain authentication for an admin who will perform the notification provider update.
Create a new notification provider in order to have a valid notificationProviderId needed for update.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to update a notification provider with a non-existent or already-deleted notificationProviderId. Ensure the system returns an appropriate error, such as not found. Requires admin authentication. No actual notification provider needs to be created as a prerequisite, but it's possible to use a deliberately invalid or non-existent UUID as the update target.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin to attempt updating a notification provider.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to change the provider_key of an existing notification provider fails validation and returns a business rule error. After authenticating as admin and creating a notification provider, attempt a PUT operation with a new provider_key. Verify that the update is rejected and the error is descriptive per business rules, ensuring referential integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as admin.
Create a notification provider to update and obtain its notificationProviderId.

scenario.draft: Test successful soft-deletion of a notification provider by admin. Start by creating and logging in as admin, then create a notification provider to obtain a valid notificationProviderId. Issue a DELETE request and verify that the provider's deleted_at timestamp is set, the provider is excluded from active provider lists in subsequent searches, and the record is retained for audit purposes. Confirm that all actions are audit-logged as per compliance policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register and log in as admin to perform operations.
Create the notification provider to be deleted.

scenario.draft: Attempt to soft-delete a notification provider that has already been deleted. After creating and deleting a provider as admin, attempt a second DELETE operation with the same notificationProviderId. Validate that the API returns a clear error indicating that the record is already deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration and authentication.
Create a test provider for delete scenario.
Perform the initial delete to set up the already-deleted state.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to delete a notification provider using a non-existent or invalid notificationProviderId. The endpoint should return a not found or similar error; no prior provider creation is necessary. Ensure business logic protects against deletion of non-existing records.

dependencies.purpose: Admin authentication to access the endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test searching operational logs with minimal filters to retrieve recent operational activities as an admin. Register and login as admin. Ensure the resulting log list contains expected records, paginates correctly, and returns all mandatory summary fields. Validate that filtering, pagination, and sorting operate as specified for the endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin to use the search endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the details of a specific operational log by operationalLogId. Register and authenticate as admin, then create a new operational log entry to obtain the ID. Perform the GET operation and verify that all expected fields (log level, message, event code, context, timestamp, actor, etc.) are returned accurately and match the created log data.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin.
Create an operational log entry to obtain a valid operationalLogId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test attempting to retrieve an operational log with a non-existent or already-deleted operationalLogId as admin. Confirm the system returns a clear error indicating record not found. This validates proper error handling for fetch and compliance access.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to access the endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new operational log by an admin. Begin by registering and logging in as admin. Call the POST endpoint with required fields (log level, message, event code, metadata). Verify that the response contains the expected log entry with all supplied data and generated metadata (timestamp, actor).

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin to perform creation of an operational log.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully soft-delete a board history event by its unique boardHistoryId. First, register a new admin and moderator via their registration endpoints, and login both users. Then, the admin creates a category and board, and assigns the moderator to the board. The moderator creates a board history event, then performs a DELETE using the event's boardHistoryId. Confirm that the board history's deleted_at is set, and that it no longer appears in standard queries, but remains accessible for audit. All steps must follow correct permission roles.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin; this is needed for all board category, board, and assignment creation.
Log the admin in to obtain credentials for protected endpoints.
Admin creates a category as a prerequisite for board creation.
Admin creates a board associated with the category, needed for moderator assignment and board history actions.
Moderator registration to perform moderator-only actions.
Moderator login to obtain required privileges for the test.
Admin assigns the moderator to the created board.
Moderator creates a board history event for the board.

scenario.draft: Test admin ability to soft-delete a board history event by its boardHistoryId. Flow: register and login as admin, create a category and board, create a board history event for the board, then issue DELETE on boardHistoryId as admin. Verify the board history is no longer available in standard queries and its deleted_at timestamp is set. Confirm actions are logged and audit/history is audit-accessible.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to perform the required admin tasks in the test.
Login the new admin in order to perform privileged operations.
Create a category for the new board that will have board histories.
Create a board under the new category for board history creation.
Create a board history entry for the test.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can search for their assigned boards using filters and pagination. The test covers success and edge cases: first, register and login as moderator and admin, create a category, a board, and assign the moderator to the board. Have the moderator query assignments with filters for moderatorId, boardId, and status, verifying that only matching assignments are returned. Test pagination and search with no results when filters do not match any assignment.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator to perform search as a logged-in moderator.
Login as moderator to search assignments.
Register a new admin for privileged actions (board setup, assignment).
Admin login for creating board/category and assigning moderator.
Admin creates a category for a new board.
Admin creates a board, required for making assignments.
Admin assigns the moderator to the new board.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can search and filter all moderator-board assignments using multiple criteria and pagination. Register and login as admin, create two moderators via their respective flows, create a category and two boards, assign each moderator to a board, and use PATCH with advanced filtering to search assignments by moderatorId, boardId, adminId, status, and pagination. Test both successful and empty result scenarios for complex, multi-criteria searches.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for all assignment/board actions.
Admin login for privileged task flows.
Create category to allow board instantiation.
Create boards for assignment events.
Create first moderator for assignment.
Login as first moderator for mod id reference.
Create second moderator for assignment.
Assign first moderator to one board.
Assign second moderator to another board.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a moderator-board assignment by ID as a logged-in moderator. After registering and logging in both moderator and admin, the admin creates a category, a board, assigns the moderator, and returns the assignmentId. The moderator retrieves the assignment by {moderatorBoardAssignmentId}, expecting assignment details for a valid ID. Then, attempt to fetch with a random/non-existent assignmentId and confirm a not found/forbidden error is returned. Also, ensure moderators only see assignments they are authorized to view.

dependencies.purpose: Moderator sign-up for authorization.
Moderator login to perform get by ID.
Admin registration to perform pre-requisite steps.
Login as admin to create board and make assignments.
Create category for new board.
Board creation for use in assignment.
Assign moderator to board, generating an assignmentId.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can successfully retrieve full details of a specific vote on a comment. Steps: (1) Register a moderator, login to obtain moderator token. (2) Register a member, login as member, create a post and add a comment. (3) Have the member cast a vote on the comment. (4) As moderator, fetch the vote details using commentId and voteId. Verify all fields (vote value, voter, timestamp, referential integrity) are returned. Confirm the moderator only accesses records they are permitted to view. Also check permission error if a non-moderator attempts access.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for authorization to fetch vote details using moderator-level endpoint.
Login as moderator to obtain valid JWT authorization token for request.
Register a basic member for content creation and voting tests.
Login as member to create a post and comment.
Create a post as member, providing a context for comment creation.
Create a comment on the post to be voted on by the member.
Member votes on the comment, creating the vote to be queried by the moderator.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can successfully upvote/downvote a comment and that business rules prevent multiple votes from the same member on the same comment. Steps: (1) Register and login as a member. (2) Create a post, add a comment. (3) Cast a vote (upvote or downvote) as permitted. (4) Attempt to cast a second vote as the same member on the same comment. Verify that the first attempt succeeds and the second results in a business error for duplicate voting. Additionally, ensure that voting on own comment or when banned is not allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Register member who will vote on comments.
Login as member to obtain access.
Create a post for the comment thread context.
Create a target comment to vote on.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can update their own vote on a comment (changing from upvote to downvote, or vice versa) within the allowed business rule update window. Steps: (1) Register and login as member. (2) Create post, create comment, cast initial vote. (3) Update the vote using voteId and commentId, and verify the change is reflected in the database and audit trail. (4) Attempt update after update window expiration (if enforced by business rules) or by another member, expecting error response for not authorized or update period ended.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for vote placement and update.
Login for authorized actions.
Create the post which will host the comment.
Create a comment to allow voting.
Cast the initial vote needed for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can delete (retract) their own vote from a comment and that deletion adheres to business policy (e.g., within voting window, not allowed by non-owner). Steps: (1) Register and login as member. (2) Create a post, comment, and cast a vote. (3) Delete the vote and confirm it is removed from tallies and is not queryable. (4) Attempt deletion by another member (not vote owner) and confirm error for forbidden action. (5) Optionally, attempt to delete after allowed period and confirm appropriate error policy or no effect.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will create and later delete a vote.
Login for vote/deletion permissions.
Create post for vote activity context.
Create comment to vote on.
Place initial vote for deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of complete details for a specific moderation action as a moderator. Scenario requires a moderator account with proper authentication. First, create the required entities such as a reportable post or comment, trigger a moderation action (e.g., remove, warn, escalate) as a moderator, and then use the moderationActionId to fetch and verify that all audit-trail fields, rationale, operator info, and relevant metadata are correctly returned for the moderation action. Ensure that fields match the business logic and that full details are returned for the logged-in moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Register and onboard a new moderator with a unique email, display name, and consent. Required for authenticated access to moderation endpoints.
Login as the moderator to obtain authentication tokens for protected API actions.
Trigger a new moderation action (e.g., removal or warning) to supply a valid moderationActionId for the detail lookup in this test.

scenario.draft: Test error handling when a moderator attempts to retrieve details for a moderation action that does not exist. Use a valid moderator authentication context and supply a random or previously deleted moderationActionId, then verify that the API returns a clear not-found or error status as defined in the business rules. Ensure the error message is descriptive and does not expose sensitive business internals.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for authenticated access.
Login to obtain tokens for the test.

scenario.draft: Test admin ability to retrieve all business and audit metadata for a specific moderation action. First, register and log in as an admin, create a moderation action via appropriate logic (e.g., issue warning, remove content through a report flow), and then fetch its details using the moderationActionId. Validate that all fields relevant to compliance and audit are returned and follow business policy for admin context.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for privileged API access.
Login as admin to receive authentication tokens.
Create a moderation action as admin to use its ID in the retrieval test.

scenario.draft: Test error scenario when an unauthenticated or insufficiently privileged user attempts to fetch detailed moderation action information via the admin endpoint. Verify that access is denied and the system returns a relevant error message indicating lack of authorization or privilege. Confirm no private or sensitive information is disclosed in error responses.

Test creation of a new moderation action (e.g., removal, warning, edit, or escalation) as an authenticated moderator. This requires having a reportable entity (such as a post or comment), followed by submission of all required fields in business logic—report reference, operator ID, action type, rationale, and status. Ensure the system records the new moderation action, returns all audit metadata, and that related audit logs are produced. Check that only valid business logic-compliant actions can be created, and no sensitive fields are omitted.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator required for authentication.
Login as moderator for API access.

scenario.draft: Test scenario where creation of a moderation action with invalid or missing required fields is attempted. Supply an incomplete or malformed request as a moderator, and verify that the system rejects the operation with clear, actionable validation errors (such as missing action type, invalid target, or incomplete rationale) and does not create the moderation action.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator account for authentication.
Login as moderator for API context.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new moderation action by an admin. Authenticate as admin, provide valid action context (target post/comment), specify all required business fields, and verify successful creation with proper audit-log return values. Ensure role-based creation (admin) is respected and that the created action can immediately be fetched for audit and downstream workflows.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for privileged testing.
Login to admin for authorization.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a moderation action as admin but omit required fields (e.g., rationale, action type). The API should respond with validation errors and not persist the action. Validate error message clarity and check that audit logs reflect the failed attempt as intended by compliance requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for authenticated access.
Log in to obtain authentication.

scenario.draft: Test updating the status, rationale, or correctable fields of an existing moderation action as an authenticated moderator. First, create a reportable post/comment, initiate a moderation action, and then update the moderationActionId with modified fields (e.g., changing rationale or status). Confirm that changes are applied only to allowed fields, audit logs are updated, and business state reflects updated action.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator required for test workflow.
Login as moderator for workflow.
Create a moderation action to have a modifiable moderationActionId.

scenario.draft: Test scenario where a moderator attempts to update a moderation action that either does not exist or has become immutable (locked/finalized by business rules). Verify that the update is rejected with a clear error message about invalid or unauthorized mutation and confirm that no unintended changes are made to system state.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator to access API.
Login as moderator for workflow.

scenario.draft: As an admin, retrieve detailed information about a specific report filed for a post. First, register an admin account and login to obtain the necessary permissions. Then, create a member, create a post as the member, and submit a report for the post. Finally, retrieve the report by its reportId and postId, and verify that the full report details are returned. This scenario confirms successful fetch for authorized admin with valid identifiers.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account and obtain authorization tokens for subsequent admin-level actions.
Login as the admin to receive authentication tokens.
Register a standard member to perform member actions such as post and report creation.
Login as member to create a post and report for test setup.
Member creates a post which will later be reported, ensuring valid postId for the report.
Member submits a report on the created post to generate a reportId.

scenario.draft: Test edge cases where admin tries fetching a report using invalid or non-existent postId or reportId, or with insufficient permissions. Start by registering an admin and ensuring valid login. Attempt to retrieve a report using malformed or random UUIDs for postId/reportId, and verify that appropriate 'not found', 'forbidden', or error messages are returned. This test ensures robust error handling for bad input or unauthorized access.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for test actions.
Login as admin to get tokens for admin requests.

scenario.draft: As a member, submit a report about a post. Validate that reporting is only allowed for authenticated members and that duplicate reports by the same member for the same post are prevented. The scenario proceeds as follows: First, register and login as a member. Create a post as another member account to ensure the reporting member is not the author, then submit a report (reason code and description) for the post. Verify that the report is created. Try to submit a second report as the same member for the same post and confirm the API returns a duplicate error. This tests report creation flow and de-duplication logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members: one for creating the post, one for reporting.
Login as each member to perform actions.
First member creates a new post to allow another member to report it.

scenario.draft: Test post report submission fails for unauthenticated users and for invalid reason codes. Attempt to report a post without authentication and confirm a 401 or forbidden error occurs. Then, while authenticated, try submitting reports with invalid or missing reason codes/descriptions to cause schema validation errors, confirming proper error messaging and enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: A member creates a post beforehand to ensure a valid postId is available for reporting.

scenario.draft: Check moderator role attempting to submit a report with incomplete or invalid fields (e.g., missing reason, reporting own post). Attempt to report a post authored by the same moderator, or submit with missing data, and verify that validation errors or business rule errors are returned as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator, who will create a post and then attempt to report it as self.
Login as moderator for all steps.
Moderator creates a post and then attempts to report it.

scenario.draft: As an admin, attempt to submit a new report for a post. Register as admin, login, and create a post via a member account. Submit a report for that post as the admin. Confirm the report is properly created and that all required fields are enforced. Attempt to submit another report for same post as the same admin and verify duplicate prevention is active. Also test with missing required fields or invalid post to verify business logic and error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin to obtain tokens.
Login as admin for subsequent actions.
Register member to create a post.
Login as member for post creation.
Member creates a post for admin to report.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can fetch the full editable and audit history for a specific post. Prerequisites include registering an admin account, logging in to obtain authorization, creating a member post, and generating several post edits (edits recorded in history). Scenario should ensure correct filtering and pagination behavior, return of all allowed audit metadata, and testing against a post with a rich history of edits. Includes checking empty result for posts with no edits and access denial if admin is unauthorized or improperly authenticated.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account with valid credentials to obtain admin privileges for subsequent operations.
Log in with the newly created admin to obtain valid JWT for authorized actions.
Register a member account, which is needed to create a post as a normal user.
Authenticate as the member in order to create a post in the system.
Create the original post to be used as the subject for edit history.
Generate one or more post edits to populate the edit history for the post. This must be performed after post creation and by an authorized user (the author, moderator, or admin).

scenario.draft: Validate that a post's author (member) can fetch the full detail of a single edit made to their post. Steps: member registration, login, post creation, post edit creation, then querying the postEditId as the member. Should ensure all historical edit content, rationale, actor, and timestamp fields are present, and that access control restricts viewing solely to permitted actors (author, moderator, admin).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to act as post author.
Login as member to gain authorization.
Create the base post that will be used for subsequent edits.
Create one or more edits to the post to generate edit history, returning postEditId for use in detailed fetch.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a random member (not the post author and with no moderator/admin privileges) cannot access the edit history of another member's post edit via this endpoint (403 forbidden). Steps: register post author, register a second member, create post/edit as first member, then attempt to access post edit detail as the second member.

dependencies.purpose: Register the post author.
Login as the post author.
Create a post as the author.
Create an edit to the post as the author.
Register a second member that is unrelated to the post.
Log in as the second member before making access attempt.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator can access the detail of any post edit (including those not authored by themselves), regardless of post authorship, for audit and compliance purposes. Process: register a moderator, login as moderator, produce a member post and edit, then use the moderator endpoint to retrieve the edit detail and confirm full data access including actor, content, reason, and timestamps. Should validate permission enforcement and prohibit access to non-existent edit IDs.

dependencies.purpose: Register and onboard a new moderator account.
Authenticate the moderator to receive JWT.
Register a member for normal user actions.
Login as the member for post and edit creation.
Use the member account to create a post.
Member creates a post edit to supply postEditId for moderator inspection.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve complete details for any post edit, regardless of author or moderator, confirming full permission. Scenario: create an admin, login, produce a member post and post edit, then retrieve postEditId detail as admin to confirm access. Should also validate error response for non-existent or deleted postEditId.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin user for system-level access.
Admin login to obtain authorization.
Register a standard member to author the post to be edited.
Member login to write a post.
Create the post for editing and history.
Produce one or more edits for the post so that the admin has something to review.

scenario.draft: Ensure a member can create an edit record for a post they authored. Steps: member registration, login, post creation, post edit operation. Validate correct audit, editor ID match, and that the new edit is visible in post edit history. Also cover that creating multiple edits correctly appends history entries and increments version/revision counters where relevant.

dependencies.purpose: Register member account who will author the post.
Login as the member for authorization.
Author creates a post for subsequent editing.

scenario.draft: Verify a member cannot create an edit record for a post they do not own (permission denied scenario). Steps: two separate member accounts, first creates post, second attempts to create an edit for the other's post - should return forbidden error for second member.

dependencies.purpose: Register the post author.
Login as the post author.
Create the post as first member.
Register a second (non-author) member.
Login as the second member prior to attempting the unauthorized edit.

scenario.draft: Test updating a specific incident record by its unique ID as an admin. First, register an admin account and log in to acquire the necessary authorization. Create a new incident record to obtain a valid incidentId. Attempt a successful update by changing the description or status (e.g., set it to 'resolved') and verify the changes persist in the system. Also, attempt to update immutable properties such as the incident code or creation timestamp to verify that such operations are correctly rejected with validation errors. Additionally, check that only admins are permitted to perform updates, and attempts by other roles or unauthenticated users result in appropriate permission errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to acquire admin-level system access required to update an incident.
Log in as admin to acquire a valid JWT token for authorization.
Create a new incident to obtain a valid incidentId for the update operation.

scenario.draft: Test hard deletion of an incident record by its unique incidentId as a super-admin. Begin by registering and logging in as an admin. Create an incident to ensure there is at least one incident record to delete. Attempt to delete the incident and verify it is removed from the list of incidents. Check that all related compliance, auditing, and reporting rules are enforced (e.g., mandatory logging of deletion with rationale). Test error responses for attempts to delete non-existent, already deleted, or unauthorized record deletions; ensure such attempts yield clear error messages. Validate that only an admin can perform this deletion operation and that other user types receive a permission denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a super-admin/admin user to perform the incident deletion operation.
Authenticate as the admin to perform privileged operations.
Create a new incident entry, providing a valid incidentId for the deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test searching and retrieving maintenance window events using filtering, sorting, and pagination as an admin. Register and log in as an admin first. Create multiple maintenance window records with varying codes, impact types, and time windows. Perform a search query without filters, then with specific filters such as time range, status, and code to verify correct results. Validate the pagination and sorting behaviors. Also, test edge cases such as invalid filter syntax, empty results, and permission denial for unauthenticated users.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to ensure appropriate permissions to search maintenance windows.
Admin login to obtain JWT for authorization.
Create one or more maintenance window events for search and filtering tests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a single maintenance window record by its unique ID as an admin. First, register and log in as an admin. Create a new maintenance window and use its ID to fetch the record with the GET method, ensuring the returned details match exactly what was stored. Attempt retrieval of a non-existent or deleted maintenanceWindowId and confirm the system returns a not-found error. Finally, confirm access is restricted to admins and unauthorized requests are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for authorized access.
Log in as admin to gain authorization.
Create a new maintenance window to provide a valid maintenanceWindowId for the GET test.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new maintenance window via admin endpoint. Register and log in as an admin to obtain authorization. Submit valid creation data and verify the maintenance window is correctly stored with all specified details. Attempt to create another maintenance window with conflicting or invalid input (such as overlapping windows or invalid time range) and check that the API returns the expected validation errors. Also, confirm that only admins can perform creation and unauthenticated or unauthorized requests are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin as prerequisite for maintenance window creation.
Log in as admin to obtain the JWT required for authorized creation requests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a filtered and paginated list of historical board change events as a moderator. Ensure realistic moderator authentication by registering and logging in as a moderator first. Create one or more boards (requires an admin to create categories and boards), perform board changes to generate board history records (such as moving a board to a different category or editing board metadata through the admin). Then, as an authenticated moderator, perform a PATCH request to fetch board history using various filters (by change type, actor, time range, board, category, etc.) and verify: (1) Board history returns only events moderator has access to; (2) Filters, sorting, and pagination operate as expected; (3) Edge cases such as no results, invalid filters, or forbidden access are handled with proper errors; (4) Audit compliance and operational constraints are present.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator for authentication context.
Log in as the registered moderator to perform authorized queries.
Register a new admin (needed to create board categories and boards for context data).
Admin login for authentication.
Create board categories for board creation and assignment (must precede board creation).
Create discussion boards linked to categories, so history records can exist.
Generate board history entries by performing board migration or category changes as admin.

scenario.draft: Verify admin's ability to search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of board change history events. Register and log in as admin, ensure several board changes to establish a meaningful audit log. Use a PATCH request to /polEcoBoard/admin/boardHistories with a variety of filters (change_type, actor, board, category, date interval), confirming: (1) Admin can view all relevant history entries; (2) Filtering and pagination work as specified; (3) Access is denied for unauthorized roles; (4) Robust input validation and error messaging for improper filter parameters or missing context.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for authentication context.
Admin login to obtain appropriate permissions.
Create board categories as prerequisites for board creation.
Create boards within categories so that history events can be generated.
Create board history records by performing valid structural changes as admin.

scenario.draft: Test fetching the full details of a board change history event by its ID as a moderator. Register a moderator and log in, ensure relevant board histories exist (created via admin actions), then as the moderator, call GET on /polEcoBoard/moderator/boardHistories/{boardHistoryId} using a valid history ID. Expect: (1) Moderator receives all permitted details and references (board, categories, actor, rationale); (2) Invalid or unauthorized history IDs return not found or permission error; (3) Edge case of non-existent or deleted IDs handled correctly; (4) Permission matrix is enforced – moderator only sees records according to business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator to execute authenticated requests.
Login as moderator for auth context.
Register an admin for board and history creation.
Authenticate as admin.
Create categories needed for boards.
Create boards and assign categories.
Generate board history records that can be fetched by moderator.

scenario.draft: Test the ability for a moderator to soft-delete (archive) a board status record. Register and log in as a moderator, ensure a valid board and an associated status event exist (admin must create category and board, then a moderator status event is created). As the moderator, delete the existing board status event by its ID and verify: (1) The event is marked deleted (deleted_at set); (2) Deleted event is no longer visible in active listings but retained for audit; (3) Attempts to delete non-existent, already-deleted, or unauthorized IDs return correct error responses; (4) Proper compliance logging is performed for moderation action.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for test authentication.
Moderator login for secure operations.
Admin registration for board/category creation.
Admin login for setup.
Create a category as the context for board.
Create board linked to category.
Moderator creates a board status event to set up for deletion.

scenario.draft: Verify as admin the ability to soft-delete a board status event. Register and log in as admin, ensure a board and a relevant status exist (by creating category, board, and a board status event via another admin or moderator). Then perform a DELETE on /polEcoBoard/admin/boardStatuses/{boardStatusId} to archive the status event. Validate: (1) Event is flagged with deleted_at, not physically deleted; (2) It becomes inaccessible from active board status queries; (3) Audit trail logs are updated for compliance; (4) Edge cases such as attempting to delete already-deleted or non-existent status IDs are handled safely with business-meaningful errors; (5) Action is denied for users without admin role.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for authentication context.
Admin login to establish permissions.
Create a category as prerequisite for boards.
Create discussion board used in status event.
Create a board status event as admin or by assigning a moderator, so that a status event exists for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can search and retrieve escalation records filtered by various attributes, such as status, actor, rationale, and date range. Verify that only escalations visible to the moderator (based on their role and board assignments) are returned. Ensure pagination and sorting work as intended. Test for no-result scenarios and input validation errors (e.g., invalid filter fields). Attempting to search with insufficient privileges should result in a permission error. Edge cases include very large result sets and filtering for deleted or restricted escalation records.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator account to provide authentication for escalation search.
Login as the moderator to obtain the JWT required for authenticated requests.
Create one or more escalation records as test data to validate search filters and pagination.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve full details of a specific escalation record by its escalationId, provided the record is visible within their role scope. Attempt to fetch a non-existent escalationId and verify a not-found error is returned. Attempt to access an escalation outside the moderator's assignment or privilege scope and verify that a permission denied error is provided. Edge cases should include attempting to access deleted or finalized escalations and verifying appropriate error handling and audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for authentication context.
Authenticate as the moderator.
Create escalation records by admin for association and access verification.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the detail of an escalation record by escalationId. Validate that all business and relational fields are included in the response. Attempt to fetch an escalationId that does not exist and verify the system responds with a clear not-found error. Confirm access is denied if an invalid or non-admin token is used in the request. Edge cases include requests for deleted, closed, or escalations unrelated to the current admin.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to create and access escalation records.
Login as admin for authorized session/context.
Create escalation records for test case validation.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator is able to create a new escalation event using valid data. Validations include: referencing an existing moderation action, specifying the correct escalatorId (current moderator), assigning a valid recipient admin, providing business rationale, and initializing status according to business logic. Verify rejection for non-existent target moderation actions, invalid adminId, missing rationale, or authentication failure. Duplicate or unauthorized escalation attempts (e.g., by a member or with locked moderation action) should be denied and yield appropriate error responses. Resulting record should reflect the submitted data and be available in search endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Register the moderator who will perform the escalation.
Login the moderator for session authentication.
Register an admin to act as recipient of the escalation.
Login as the admin recipient (if required for association context).
Create a sample moderation action to reference during escalation creation.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully create a new escalation event, specifying a valid moderation action, rationale, escalatorId (admin or moderator), and recipient admin. Validate required fields and verify correct handling of input errors such as missing rationale, referencing non-existent moderation actions, or invalid assignment. Ensure proper error messages are presented for each case. Confirm that the escalation record is persisted, all required metadata and relationships are established, and the event appears in downstream search and detail APIs.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin, who will perform escalation creation.
Authenticate as admin for escalation creation and target association.
Register a moderator to supply as an escalator or as the subject of moderation action.
Create a suitable moderation action record for association with the escalation event.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving detailed information for a specific board status event as a moderator. The scenario begins with the registration and login of a moderator, then a board status event is created (using moderator privileges), and finally the status is retrieved by its boardStatusId. Key verifications include successful retrieval when the event exists and proper permissions, error response when the boardStatusId does not exist, and forbidden access for users with insufficient permissions (non-moderator, non-admin roles). Also test access to already deleted or soft-deleted status events.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account for permission to create and access board status events.
Login as moderator to obtain necessary authentication token.
Create a new board status event and obtain the boardStatusId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new board status event as a moderator. The scenario should cover: 1) successful creation with valid data (after moderator registration and login), 2) creation attempt with missing or invalid required fields (such as missing boardId, invalid status type, or missing rationale), 3) creation with reference to a non-existent board, and 4) forbidden or unauthorized attempts by a non-moderator role. Also, ensure business rules such as status-type transitions are enforced, and error messages are descriptive.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator account to be able to create a board status event.
Login as moderator to obtain authentication for creating events.
Create a board as a prerequisite for a valid boardId reference when testing valid creation scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a board status event as an admin user. This scenario includes: 1) successful creation after registering and logging in as admin, 2) input validation failure (e.g., missing rationale or invalid status type), 3) attempt to create status for a non-existent board, 4) verifying that admin-only events cannot be performed by users with lower roles, and 5) business rule errors such as status transition not allowed. Additionally, validate audit logging and rationale requirements are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account for privileged board status events.
Login as admin to allow creating board statuses.
Establish a valid board for status creation and boardId referencing.

scenario.draft: Test updating details of an existing board status event as a moderator. Scenarios include: 1) successful update when boardStatusId exists and the moderator is authorized, 2) attempt to update with invalid or missing fields, 3) attempt to update an event after allowed edit window (if applicable), 4) updating a deleted or non-existent status event, and 5) permission errors when performed by non-moderators. Ensure audit trail is updated accordingly and business rules for allowed updates are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator for performing update operations.
Login as moderator to obtain authentication token.
Create a board status event and obtain boardStatusId that will be updated.

scenario.draft: Test the admin update of a board status event for compliance and operational changes. Begin by registering and logging in as admin, then create a board and associated board status. Test cases should include: 1) valid update by admin (e.g., correcting rationale or time), 2) validation errors for missing/invalid fields, 3) update attempts on soft-deleted or non-existent status events, 4) permission error for non-admin roles, and 5) verify that changes are correctly reflected in audit logs and business rules regarding editability are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to perform status updates.
Login as admin to get authentication token.
Create a board so a valid board status can be associated and created.
Create board status event using admin privileges to obtain boardStatusId.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of an existing maintenance window by admin. Start with admin registration and login to obtain credentials. Create a new maintenance window via POST to get a valid maintenanceWindowId. Execute PUT with modified fields (e.g., updated start/end time, updated impact description, notification timestamps). Verify the response contains updated fields, audit log is appended, and inference checks for time window and policy are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to obtain permissions for maintenance operations.
Authenticate as the registered admin to obtain a JWT for subsequent requests.
Create a new maintenance window to supply a valid maintenanceWindowId for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when start time is after end time, which violates business logic. Begin with admin registration, login, and creation of a maintenance window. Attempt to update the maintenance window by submitting a payload where the start time is after the end time. Check that the response returns a validation error, and that the record is not updated.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for API authentication.
Login as the admin to authorize requests.
Create a maintenance window in advance to retrieve a valid maintenanceWindowId.

scenario.draft: Test admin ability to soft-delete (archive) a maintenance window. Perform admin registration, login, and create a maintenance window. Then, call DELETE on the new maintenanceWindowId. Assert that the deleted_at field is set, the maintenance window is marked as deleted, and that subsequent retrievals or listings do not include the deleted window (unless filter includes deleted).

dependencies.purpose: Provision a new admin account for permissioned API access.
Authenticate as admin to enable authorized actions.
Establish a maintenance window to obtain a valid maintenanceWindowId for deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test admin ability to search and paginate service metrics with various combinations of filters and sorting. After registering and logging in as admin, create several service metrics records using POST. Use PATCH to search with different query parameters (e.g., filtering by metric_code, date range, or sorting by created date). Validate that the correct filtered subset and pagination structures are returned, including metadata about total records and pages.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for permissions.
Obtain an authenticated session as admin.
Add multiple service metric records so the search endpoint returns non-empty results.

scenario.draft: Test the successful retrieval of a single service metric's full details by an admin. Perform admin registration, login, and create a service metric record, then make a GET request referencing its serviceMetricId. Confirm the returned object matches the created record, including all summary and detail fields. Verify proper error handling if a non-existent or deleted serviceMetricId is used.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin privileges for secure endpoints.
Ensure authenticated admin session.
Create a new service metric to generate and retrieve a valid serviceMetricId for detail testing.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a service metric by an authenticated admin. After admin registration and login, use POST with valid metric_code, value, window, and all required fields consistent with schema rules. Confirm that the record is saved and all validations (uniqueness per code/time, value type) are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user to enable metric record creation.
Login as admin to acquire JWT authentication context.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of an admin to search and retrieve a paginated list of discussion boards with advanced filters. Ensure filtering works by category ID, board code, display name, status, and display order. Verify sorting and pagination (page, limit) return correct data slices. Include edge case testing for empty results, non-existent filters (e.g., invalid category), invalid pagination values, and that only boards linked to existing categories are returned. Proper permission enforcement is expected, and non-admin access should be denied. Results must provide the expected board schema details and reflect current database state.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account. Only admins can access this search endpoint.
Log in as an admin to obtain credentials for subsequent requests.
Create at least one board category for use as a valid filter and to link boards to this category. This precedes board creation and search.
Create one or more boards, referencing the created categories, to test the filtering/search functionality.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of a specific discussion board by its unique boardId. Prepare a board via the creation endpoint, then request its detail using the GET endpoint. Verify that the response contains all business fields: id, category link, board name, code, description, visibility, archive status, display order, and timestamps. Negative scenarios: attempt retrieval with a non-existent boardId (should return not found error), use an invalid UUID format (should return validation error), and attempt access as non-admin (should return forbidden/permission-denied error).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for authentication.
Admin login for permissioned access.
Create a category; required for board creation.
Create a board to provide a valid boardId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test board creation by an admin with both valid and invalid input data. For success, provide a valid categoryId, board name (2–60 chars), unique code (2–30 chars, lowercase/underscored), description, visibility, archive state, and display order. Verify response matches the persisted DTO. For failure scenarios: supply non-existent categoryId (should return referential integrity error), duplicate board name or code (should return uniqueness error), missing/invalid required fields (should return validation errors), and attempt creation as non-admin (should return forbidden). Ensure business rules such as linkage to valid category and uniqueness are fully validated.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin account to gain board creation privileges.
Admin login to obtain authorization.
Create a category to use its categoryId when creating the board.

scenario.draft: Test updating a discussion board by id as an admin. Cover success scenario by changing fields such as category, board name/code, description, public/archive flags, and display order with valid data—confirm response reflects changes accurately. Test edge cases: updating with duplicate name or code (should return uniqueness conflict), invalid category id (should fail with referential integrity error), updating with missing required fields (should fail with descriptive error), and using non-existent boardId (should return not found). Also verify that permission is enforced (non-admins cannot update a board) and audit trail/logging is maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for update privileges.
Authenticate as admin for authorized requests.
Create at least two categories to allow board category changes in the update process.
Create a board instance to provide a target for the update.

scenario.draft: Test the soft delete (archive) of a board by boardId as an admin. On success, ensure the deleted_at field is set and the board is not shown in active listings but remains for audit and possible restoration. Edge cases include: deleting a non-existent or already deleted board (should return appropriate error), attempting delete with insufficient permissions (non-admins or unauthorized roles should fail), and verifying the business logic constraints (cannot delete a board that does not meet certain criteria, e.g., if referenced in a mandatory workflow, should be blocked). All delete actions must be fully audited.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to access the delete endpoint.
Admin login for permissioned operations.
Create a category to allow board creation.
Create a board that will be targeted for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test viewing a notification as a moderator. First, register a new moderator and log in to obtain a JWT token. Next, create a notification assigned to that moderator using the admin API. Retrieve the notification using the moderator's token and verify all appropriate metadata is returned, access is allowed, and privacy protections are enforced. Also, attempt to access a notification with an invalid or unauthorized ID, and as a non-owner, confirming correct error handling for not-found and forbidden cases.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account with valid details. Required for any moderator-level operations.
Log in as the newly registered moderator to obtain JWT for authentication.
Register a new admin account for admin-level operations.
Log in as admin to obtain admin JWT for notification creation.
Create a notification event assigned to the moderator. Used as the target in view scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test admin access for notification records. Register and log in as admin. Create several notification events targeting different members and moderators. Fetch individual notifications by their IDs and confirm all metadata and business fields are present, including delivery and event status. Test access to both valid and invalid IDs, including attempting to retrieve a notification that does not belong to the admin or does not exist, ensuring appropriate error responses are given.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account, required for all admin role scenarios.
Log in as admin and obtain credentials for subsequent API calls.
Create notification records to test retrieval and permission boundaries.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a notification event by an admin. Register and log in as an admin. Attempt to create notification records using valid data for event type, recipient, and status, and verify successful creation with correct returned fields. Next, attempt to create notifications with missing required fields, invalid event types, or non-existent recipient IDs, and check that validation errors are returned with descriptive messages as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account so that notification creation is permitted.
Authenticate as admin to obtain required credentials for notification creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating a notification as a member. First, register a new member and log in to obtain credentials. Create a notification via the admin for this member. Attempt to update permissible fields in the notification and verify success, audit trail, and correct response structure. Test failure scenarios by trying to update a notification not belonging to the member, or supplying invalid values (unsupported event_type or status), and ensure the API enforces permissions and input validation.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member account for use as the notification recipient.
Log in as the member to obtain authentication token for updates.
Register an admin to allow notification creation.
Admin login, required to create notifications for the member.
Create a notification for the member, which will be used in update and error scenarios.

scenario.draft: Validate notification update functionality for a moderator. Register and log in as a moderator. Admin creates a notification assigned to this moderator. Update allowed notification properties as moderator and verify all changes persist, status updates are reflected, and changes are properly audited. Also, attempt to update notifications that belong to other accounts or supply invalid updates (such as improper statuses or unsettable fields), and confirm proper error handling and access controls.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator, needed for moderator-authenticated API usage.
Obtain moderator JWT for authorization.
Set up an admin for notification event creation.
Log in as admin to create notifications for moderators.
Create one or more notifications for the moderator, as the target of update actions.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully update allowed metadata fields (such as context or compliance note) for an existing account audit record. The scenario starts by registering a new admin, logging in, creating an account audit record for a target, and then issuing a PUT with updated compliance metadata. Confirm the returned object reflects the changed values and audit history is preserved. Required ordering: admin registration -> login -> create account audit -> update.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to allow account audit update operations.
Login as admin to obtain valid authentication for update.
Create an initial account audit record to produce a valid accountAuditId for updating.

scenario.draft: Ensure that non-admin users (such as members or moderators) are forbidden from updating account audit records. Begin by registering a member, logging in, then attempting a PUT to update an account audit record (created by admin) and expect a permission error. This tests strict access control at the API layer.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new regular member for the negative permission test.
Login as member to attempt forbidden update.
Create an account audit record (as admin) used in update attempt.

scenario.draft: Test the ability for an admin to hard delete an account audit record by its unique ID. The scenario requires creating a new admin, logging in, creating an account audit record, then calling DELETE on the record and confirming it no longer appears in search results. Ensure audit logging is verified for the deletion action as well.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin, required for performing delete operations.
Login as admin to obtain authentication/context for delete.
Create an account audit record to obtain accountAuditId for deletion.
Search audits to confirm soft/hard delete effects after operation.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempts by non-admin roles (regular member or moderator) to delete an account audit event are strictly forbidden. Set up a member, login, attempt to delete a valid admin-created account audit record, and confirm a permission-denied error is returned. This scenario tests access controls for sensitive audit logs.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for non-admin access test.
Login as member to attempt unauthorized delete.
Create a real audit log for delete attempt.

scenario.draft: Admins can successfully search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of board status events with flexible filter criteria such as boardId, status type, actor, and date range. Ensure the response respects pagination, and contains only board statuses visible to admin. Create a test board and board status, then query with patch. Validates result structure and access.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for full access to search endpoint.
Login as admin for search authentication.
Create a new category for board association.
Create a board associated with the category to allow creation of board status.
Create a board status event to populate data for searching.

scenario.draft: Validate that the search endpoint returns an empty result set when filters do not match any board status records (e.g., random UUID for boardId or status type that doesn't exist). This confirms behavior for empty datasets and result consistency under strict filters.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin to be able to call the search endpoint.
Admin login provides authentication context.

scenario.draft: Moderators should only see board statuses associated with boards they are assigned to, or as allowed by business rules. Register a moderator, create board(s), assign moderator to the board, issue board status changes, and verify on search that only appropriate records are visible according to assignment and role filters. Scenario steps: moderator registration -> login -> create category/board -> assign moderator -> create board status -> patch search.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator to test moderator-level board status search.
Login as moderator for authentication.
Create a category for associating to a board.
Create a board for moderator assignment and board status events.
Assign the moderator to the board allowing scoped access.
Create a board status as the assigned moderator.

scenario.draft: Admin user is able to retrieve detailed business and audit information for a specific board status by ID. Register an admin, login, create category and board, create a board status, then fetch its details by ID, confirming all fields and references are correct and permissions are enforced. Sequence is critical to generate a valid boardStatusId to test details endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to permit board status creation and detail lookup.
Admin login to get authentication context.
Create a category for the board to belong to.
Create a board that will receive status events.
Create a board status entry to generate a real boardStatusId for GET by ID test.

scenario.draft: Test the successful issuance of a new JWT access and refresh token for an admin user when a valid, unexpired refresh token is supplied. The test must first register a new admin, log them in to obtain the initial refresh token, then invoke the refresh endpoint with that token. It must verify that the new tokens are different from the previous ones and that setHeaders are returned. All business and security rules for session renewal must be validated.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to enable authentication-required operations. This must be completed first for admin existence.
Log in with the registered admin to obtain the initial access and refresh tokens required for the refresh scenario.

scenario.draft: Test failure scenario where an admin attempts to use an expired or explicitly revoked refresh token to obtain new JWT tokens. After registering and logging in as admin to get valid tokens, simulate expiry (or explicitly revoke via logout), then attempt to refresh using the now-invalid token. Validate that the operation is rejected with a clear and actionable error message, and that security rules prevent a new session from being issued.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin so that a valid refresh token can be generated for testing revoked/expired scenarios.
Log in as the admin and obtain the tokens to test.
Revoke the refresh token by logging out prior to testing refresh. This ensures token is no longer valid for refresh attempts.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of all active sessions belonging to the logged-in admin account. Register and authenticate as an admin, perform one or more logins (if possible from distinct contexts), and then call the sessions endpoint to verify that only the current admin's active sessions are returned, each with correct metadata and no unauthorized information.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account so that session enumeration can be tested in a valid authentication context.
Obtain a valid access token to authorize session list retrieval.

scenario.draft: Verify that attempting to enumerate admin sessions without a valid admin authentication JWT is strictly rejected. Attempt session listing with no token or using a non-admin token and verify that an appropriate 401 or 403 error response is returned, and no sensitive data is leaked.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular member to confirm non-admin access is denied for session enumeration.
Login as the member to obtain a member JWT and attempt unauthorized access.

scenario.draft: Test admin's ability to revoke a specific active session by sessionId. Register and log in as admin on multiple devices (sessions) if possible, enumerate active sessions, and delete one session by its ID. Confirm that the session is revoked (cannot be used) and other unaffected sessions remain active. Check that audit/compliance logs (if available) reflect the session revocation.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin and create multiple sessions for real revocation test context.
Login from separate contexts to create multiple session records.
Enumerate all active sessions to get a sessionId to test revocation on.

scenario.draft: Attempt to revoke a session using an invalid or unauthorized sessionId (e.g., one that does not belong to the current admin or does not exist). The test expects a not found or unauthorized response, with no effect on valid sessions. Ensures business logic prohibits session manipulation across accounts and handles errors securely.

dependencies.purpose: Set up admin account context for attempting invalid deletions.
Obtain access in order to test session revocation with fabricated or unrelated IDs.

scenario.draft: Test complete logout (revocation) of all active authentication sessions for the logged-in admin. Register and log in as admin (potentially multiple times from different browsers to create multiple sessions), then call the revoke-all endpoint. Confirm that all sessions are invalidated and cannot be used, and that re-login is required. This is essential for enterprise-grade security incident handling.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin and create active sessions to enable global session revocation test.
Launch multiple login sessions for the same admin for effective testing of mass logout.

scenario.draft: Test the successful update of a consent status record by an admin. The scenario begins with registering an admin account and logging in to obtain authorization. Next, create a sample consent status record to ensure data is available for update. Then, perform a PUT request on the /polEcoBoard/admin/consentStatuses/{consentStatusId} endpoint to amend a legal consent status field, such as the consent_status or audit metadata, ensuring the update operation is properly reflected. Validate that the resulting consent status entity is returned with the updated field values, and all changes are correctly logged for compliance. Business logic such as permitted and immutable fields should be enforced by the API.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account, enabling access to privileged endpoints.
Log in as the created admin to acquire an authentication token required for authorized requests.
Create a consent status record to provide a valid consentStatusId for the update scenario.

scenario.draft: Test rejection of a consent status update attempt by an admin using fields that are not permitted to be modified, such as immutable identifiers or non-existent fields. After setting up an admin and a valid consent status record, use the endpoint with invalid update payload data. The API should return an error indicating which fields are not modifiable per compliance policy. This ensures audit integrity and legal correctness.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin user to obtain authorization for the operation.
Admin logs in to obtain the session token for authorized calls.
Create a consent status entry to offer a valid record for faulty update attempts.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where an admin attempts to update a consent status that does not exist (invalid consentStatusId). After admin registration and authentication, submit the update request to a non-existent or deleted consentStatusId. The system should respond with a not_found error and descriptive message, verifying that the update does not affect any records and compliance is maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Setup an admin account for access control.
Administrator login needed for authorization.

scenario.draft: Test the successful permanent deletion of a consent status record by an admin. This includes registering and logging in an admin, creating a new consent status entry, then issuing a DELETE request to /polEcoBoard/admin/consentStatuses/{consentStatusId}. The system should remove the record permanently and log the deletion for compliance. Confirm that subsequent fetch attempts receive not_found responses, and attempt deletion of already-deleted records results in appropriate errors.

dependencies.purpose: Admin account registration to ensure proper permission.
Admin authentication to acquire a valid session for authorized API calls.
Create a consent status record, providing a target consentStatusId for the delete scenario.

scenario.draft: Test the consent status delete operation with a non-existent consentStatusId. After authenticating as admin, execute DELETE on a random or previously removed consentStatusId. Confirm the system returns an explicit not_found error and does not affect any existing records. This ensures compliance with privacy law and data retention requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for proper privileges.
Authenticate as admin to access protected endpoints.

scenario.draft: Test searching for notification providers as an admin. Register and log in as admin to obtain an authentication token. Execute a PATCH request with a variety of filters (e.g., by status or region) or without filters (fetching all providers). Validate that results are paginated, correctly filtered/sorted as per the request, and match the pol_eco_board_notification_providers schema. Confirm access is admin-restricted.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin account for credentialed access.
Admin login to obtain authentication for the search.
Create at least one provider to ensure results exist for search scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test the system's response to invalid search filter parameters. After admin setup, perform a PATCH with clearly invalid search/filter parameters (e.g., unsupported field names or values out of range). Confirm that the API returns a descriptive error and does not return confidential provider data, ensuring robust input validation.

dependencies.purpose: Enable administrative privileges for the search operation.
Obtain token/session for privileged calls.

scenario.draft: Test that non-admin users are forbidden from accessing the provider search endpoint. Register a member, log in as that user, and attempt PATCH /polEcoBoard/admin/notificationProviders. System should return a permission/authorization error, and no data should be exposed. This enforces security boundaries and data privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Create a standard member account which should not be permitted to search providers.
Member login to acquire a session for use in unauthorized calls.

scenario.draft: Test successfully fetching details for a specific notification provider as an admin. Register and log in as admin, create a provider record, then use the /polEcoBoard/admin/notificationProviders/{notificationProviderId} endpoint to fetch the record.
