scenario.draft: Test searching for reports on a comment as a moderator, filtering by status, report reason, and reporter ID. Validate correct pagination and that the reports returned are only those matching the filter criteria. Ensure access includes all reports for the comment regardless of status (open, resolved, invalid). Provide both successful (results and empty) and error (invalid commentId, unauthorized) cases. Moderator registration and login must precede this test, as search access requires moderator privileges.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account to obtain a moderator ID and credentials.
Login with the moderator credentials to obtain access tokens for subsequent moderator-auth operations.
Create a post as a member to which the comment will be attached.
Create a comment as a member that can be reported and searched for reports.
Generate one or more reports on the comment to have data to search.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can search, paginate, and filter all abuse/activity reports linked to a specific comment. Use advanced filters such as report reason, status, reporter ID, time range, and verify the admin sees all relevant report metadata. Include successful result case, filter producing empty results, and error scenarios like invalid commentId and insufficient privileges. Admin registration and login are required prior to running this test, since admin authorization is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account with full platform privileges.
Login as the registered admin to obtain the admin JWT for authorized actions.
Set up a post as a member so a comment can be created and reported.
Create a target comment within the post to be reported.
File one or more reports on the comment so that the search results can be verified.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific report on a comment as a moderator, including all moderation and reporter metadata. The scenario should verify that the moderator can access the report detail, sees any private notes, the report reason, and reporter identity. Include query of valid report (success), invalid or unauthorized access (nonexistent or mismatched commentId/reportId, or when trying with a member account), and permission edge cases. Precondition: at least one report must exist on a test comment, with moderator authentication established prior to request.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator account for use in moderator operations.
Login as moderator to obtain required JWT for access.
Create a post so a comment can be made.
Create a comment under that post.
File a report on the comment, capturing reportId for later retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully retrieve a single report for a comment by reportId, including all associated fields such as report reason, status, description, reporter info, moderation fields, etc. The scenario covers positive retrieval, report not found, mismatched reportId/commentId, and rejected access (by another role). Admin authentication must be in place prior to attempting the fetch, and the comment must have at least one report filed beforehand.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to enable privileged operations.
Login as newly created admin to secure an access token.
Create a post so that a comment can be added.
Add a comment to the post.
Submit a report on the created comment and extract reportId for the detail query.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of a logged-in member to retrieve a paginated, filtered list of post summaries based on various filter criteria, including category, keywords in title or body, tag, creation date, and status (active/unflagged). Verify that only posts accessible to the member are returned, response contains correct pagination metadata, and business logic around visibility is enforced. Validate the search returns expected results per filters and member does not see flagged/deleted posts unless authorized. Edge cases include empty result set and page bounds exceeded.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to perform authenticated search operations as a member.
Authenticate as newly registered member to obtain JWT for authorized requests.

scenario.draft: Validate that attempts to use the member posts PATCH search endpoint without authentication (i.e., as a guest or with an expired JWT) are rejected with an appropriate unauthorized error message. Confirm that the error response is clear and that no post data is leaked.

Test the retrieval of third-party integration audit logs using multiple filters and pagination options as an authenticated admin. Verify filtering by provider key, event type, and time range returns correct audit log records. Confirm pagination metadata (next page, total count) is consistent with expected results. Also test empty results by using non-matching/invalid filters. Ensure access control prevents non-admin access and error messages are precise and actionable upon invalid query parameters.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account for use in authentication and session establishment. Required for obtaining admin role access.
Admin login to acquire authorization tokens for authenticated requests to admin-only endpoints.
Create several third-party audit log records with diverse provider keys, event types, and timestamps; necessary to ensure a meaningful data set for search and filter scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test fetching detailed information about a particular third-party audit log by its unique ID as an authenticated admin. Confirm that all audit metadata fields are present and correct. Also attempt to access a non-existent or previously deleted log and verify that a descriptive not-found error is returned. Access control must prevent non-admin users from viewing audit log details.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration, required to create accounts with sufficient permissions.
Authenticate admin and retrieve session token for subsequent API calls.
Create a third-party audit log entry to provide a valid ID for detail retrieval testing.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a new third-party integration audit log entry as an authenticated admin. Provide valid provider_key, event_type, event_payload, and result_code; confirm a successful response and correct metadata is returned. Attempt creation with missing required fields or invalid field formats to verify business validation and receive clear error messages. Test that unauthorized (non-admin) attempts are rejected, confirming permission rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to ensure valid admin credentials are available.
Authenticate as admin to obtain credentials enabling authorized third-party audit log creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating fields (event_type, result_code, event_payload, correlation_id) of an existing third-party audit log as an authenticated admin. Confirm that valid updates persist correctly. Attempt invalid field updates or updates on a deleted/immutable log to confirm business constraint enforcement and precise error responses. Test permission error when attempting update as non-admin.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration to create an account eligible for audit log operations.
Admin authentication for authorized access.
Insert an initial third-party audit log entry to be updated in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deleting a third-party integration audit log as an admin. Validate that the log is excluded from operational queries but remains for compliance. Confirm deleted logs cannot be loaded via GET (404/not found) and repeated delete requests yield clear error messages. Ensure only admins can perform deletion and unprivileged users receive proper permission errors.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration to establish credentials for authorized API usage.
Login as admin to obtain tokens for protected endpoint access.
Insert a third-party audit log entry to provide a valid target for deletion testing.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of an existing audit trail record by an admin. First, ensure an admin account is created and authenticated. Then, create an audit trail record to be updated. Execute the PUT operation to update the permissible fields of the audit trail, such as context or note. Verify that the response includes the updated audit trail record reflecting the new values and that the immutable fields remain unchanged. Confirm that an audit entry for the update is automatically created for compliance logging.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to obtain credentials with proper permissions.
Authenticate as an admin to acquire a valid JWT token for authorization.
Create an audit trail record which will be updated in this test scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that a non-admin user cannot update an audit trail record. First, register a member (non-admin) account and authenticate. Attempt to update an existing audit trail record via the PUT endpoint as a member. The API should return a permission denied or unauthorized error, and no changes should be made to the audit trail record.

dependencies.purpose: Register a regular (non-admin) member account.
Authenticate the member to obtain a JWT token.
Register an admin to create the audit trail record.
Login as admin to create the audit trail record only.
Create the audit trail entry to be used for the update attempt.

scenario.draft: Test updating a non-existent audit trail record by admin. Register and authenticate as an admin. Attempt to update an audit trail record using a random or deleted auditTrailId. The system should return an appropriate not-found error and no record should be updated or created.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account with sufficient privileges.
Login as admin to acquire a valid JWT token.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully hard-delete a specific audit trail entry by its unique ID. First, register and authenticate an admin. Create a new audit trail record. Perform the DELETE operation and verify that the record is permanently removed from the system. Validate that subsequent attempts to fetch the deleted record fail with a not-found error. All deletion actions should be appropriately logged for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to ensure operation is performed with correct privileges.
Authenticate as admin to obtain valid admin JWT session.
Create an audit trail entry to be deleted in the scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that non-admin users (e.g., members) cannot delete an audit trail entry. Register and login as a regular member. Attempt to delete an existing audit trail record using the member's credentials. The system must return a permission denied or forbidden response, and the audit trail should remain intact.

dependencies.purpose: Register a non-admin member.
Login as member to obtain a JWT token.
Register an admin needed to create the audit trail.
Login as admin to create the audit trail.
Admin creates the audit trail record to be used in this test.

scenario.draft: Assess system response when attempting to delete a non-existent audit trail record by admin. Register and authenticate as an admin, then attempt to delete an auditTrailId that does not exist (random UUID). The API should return an appropriate not-found error and no records should be affected. This ensures compliance with regulatory retention expectations.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account with deletion privileges.
Authenticate the admin to obtain a JWT session.

scenario.draft: Test successful search and pagination of incident records as an admin. Register and authenticate an admin, create multiple incident records, then perform a PATCH request to search for incidents specifying pagination and filter criteria. Verify that the results reflect the provided filters, correct pagination metadata (e.g., total count, page size), and all available records match expected shapes. Also confirm that filtering by code, status, or category returns appropriate subsets.

dependencies.purpose: Setup admin user authorized for incident search.
Login as admin for incident creation and search.
Create multiple incident records to test index and pagination.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of an incident detail by admin. Register and authenticate as admin. Create a new incident record. Fetch the incident by its unique identifier using the GET endpoint. Verify the returned details match the created incident (code, category, status, description, etc.) and that no sensitive data is improperly exposed. Confirm that the admin-only permission is enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Provide admin credentials for the test.
Authenticate as admin.
Create an incident to fetch by ID.

scenario.draft: Verify appropriate error handling when fetching a non-existent incident by ID. Register and login as admin. Attempt to fetch an incident using a random or deleted incidentId value. Assert that the API returns a clear not-found error message, and no incident details are leaked or returned.

dependencies.purpose: Setup admin user needed for the request.
Authenticate as admin.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully create a new incident record with required attributes like code, category, and description. Register and authenticate as admin. Submit a new incident record via POST. Verify that the returned record contains the code, category, detected timestamp, and any required status fields initialized appropriately. Confirm audit logging of the creation event and adherence to uniqueness constraints on incident code. Attempt to create a duplicate code to confirm expected error handling for business rule enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for authentication.
Authenticate as admin to access the incident creation feature.

scenario.draft: Verify that non-admin users are not permitted to create incident records. Register a member (non-admin) and attempt to submit a POST request to create an incident. The system should deny the operation with a permission error and not create the incident. This scenario ensures enforcement of admin-only creation rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register a non-admin member.
Authenticate as the member.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a paginated, filtered list of votes for a post as an admin. Steps: Register an admin account and log in. Have a member register, log in, and create a post. Multiple users vote (upvote/downvote) on this post. As an admin, use the endpoint to fetch votes for the post with filters (vote_value, voter_member_id) and pagination. Validate that returned results match votes cast and that analytics fields are accurate. Verify pagination works as expected when result count exceeds page limit.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account for permission to access the admin endpoint.
Admin logs in to receive authentication for API usage.
Register a member account to create test data and post content.
Member logs in to be able to create a post and vote.
Create a post on which votes will be cast and searched.
Member users cast upvote and downvote on the created post to simulate vote history for admin review.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can retrieve their own vote for a post using the voteId. Steps: Register as a member, log in, create a post, cast a vote on the post, then retrieve the vote by voteId. Verify the details match what was cast. Next, test error scenarios: try retrieving a vote by an invalid or non-existent voteId, and attempt to retrieve a vote that belongs to another user. Validate that proper error responses or permission denial are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register for member account so a post can be created and voted on.
Log in as member for authentication.
Create a post for voting.
Cast a vote (upvote/downvote); retrieve voteId for lookup test.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve any vote record by postId and voteId. Steps: Create an admin account and log in. Register a member(s), log in, create a post, cast several votes. As admin, use the endpoint to retrieve all votes using each voteId and confirm details are accessible (even if the voter is a different user). Simulate attempting to retrieve a non-existent or invalid voteId and ensure the correct error response. Also, have a non-admin attempt this endpoint and verify access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for access to the admin-only endpoint.
Admin log in to gain permission.
Register member account(s) for generating posts and votes.
Log in as member to use voting functions.
Create a post for voting.
Members cast votes so admin can review.

scenario.draft: Test member vote creation on a post, including business logic for duplicate voting and voting on own post. Steps: Member registers and logs in, creates a post, then attempts to vote on their own post (should fail). Register a second member, log in, and cast an upvote (should succeed). Try to vote again on the same post as the same member (should be disallowed by duplicate vote rule). Validate correct error messaging for business rule enforcement. Test also for vote value validation: try invalid vote_value and confirm expected validation error.

dependencies.purpose: Register both the post author and a second member for vote testing.
Both members log in to perform necessary actions.
Author creates a post for voting.

scenario.draft: Test successful admin registration and duplicate email handling. First, verify that admin registration succeeds when providing a unique email and valid password, receiving tokens for immediate access. Then, attempt to register another admin with the same email and confirm the system rejects duplication with an appropriate error. This workflow ensures uniqueness constraints and onboarding compliance. Dependencies include the admin registration endpoint for the initial registration setup.

Test admin registration failure due to insufficient password complexity. Attempt to register a new admin with a weak password that does not meet business security requirements, and validate that the API returns a specific error message indicating password constraints. This scenario validates enforcement of password security policy at registration.

Test successful login for a previously registered admin and failure for invalid credentials. Register an admin account, then attempt to log in with correct credentials and ensure access tokens are issued. Then, repeat with an incorrect password and confirm the system returns an authentication failure error. This ensures credential validation and proper session management. The login operation depends on a prior successful admin registration to provide valid credentials.

dependencies.purpose: Provides the unique admin account required for login testing. Must be executed first to supply valid credentials for authentication.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated admin can log out, which should invalidate their current session. Register and log in as an admin, then use a valid Authorization header to call logout. Afterward, verify that the JWT token used for logout can no longer access protected endpoints, confirming session revocation. This scenario requires prior admin registration and login to set up session and credentials.

dependencies.purpose: Creates the admin account to be logged in and tested.
Establishes a logged-in session with valid JWT for logout test.

scenario.draft: Test validation of admin JWT tokens. Register and log in an admin to obtain a valid token, then call the validate endpoint to confirm valid session status and admin privileges. Afterwards, provide an expired or revoked token (such as after logout) and confirm validation returns non-authenticated or error status. This ensures the endpoint correctly verifies both valid and invalid token states. Dependencies include registration, login, and logout flows for generating authentic token states.

dependencies.purpose: Provides the admin account for testing token validation.
Grants a valid token for successful validation test.
Ensures a token is revoked and can be tested as invalid in validation step.

scenario.draft: Test both successful password change for an authenticated admin and error handling for incorrect current password. Register and login as an admin, call the change password endpoint with a valid current password and acceptable new password, ensuring password is updated and all sessions are revoked (requiring re-authentication). Then, attempt to change password again with an incorrect current password and validate a specific error is returned. This confirms business logic for password change, security policy enforcement, and error scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Creates initial admin credentials.
Authenticates the admin prior to password update tests.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of the current platform-wide service settings by an authenticated admin user. The scenario includes registering a new admin account, logging in as that admin, and ensuring a valid admin JWT is used when calling this endpoint. Successful response should include all business-critical platform settings, and data should reflect the latest settings in the database.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to enable admin-level access for service settings.
Authenticate as the newly created admin to obtain a valid JWT token required for authorized admin API access.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of service settings with an invalid or expired admin JWT token. After registering and logging in as an admin, purposely use an invalid/expired token when calling this endpoint. Verify that the API returns an appropriate authorization error and does not leak sensitive platform config data.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to set up an admin account.
Obtain a valid JWT for initial admin authentication. Used to later simulate and manipulate invalid/expired tokens for test case.

scenario.draft: Test successful GET of all global platform-level settings by an authenticated admin user. This includes registering and logging in as an admin, then calling the GET endpoint. Assert that all key platform settings are present, data matches with the backend, and sensitive info is correctly included for admin context.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin account required to access the settings GET endpoint.
Log in as the admin to receive a JWT for subsequent authorized API access.

scenario.draft: Test handling of missing or deleted service settings record. After authenticating as an admin, simulate or trigger a missing singleton record in the settings table and verify the API returns a clear error message that the global settings record does not exist, to ensure safe system behavior and transparent administrative error reporting.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to gain access for the retrieval operation.
Login as the admin user for privileged access context.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of global service settings by an authenticated admin. Register and login as admin, retrieve the existing settings object, then update one or more fields (such as max_post_length or registration_enabled). Verify that the response reflects the updated values and updated_at timestamp increments. Confirm all changes are properly validated and audited.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user with authority to update global settings.
Login as the admin user to obtain the JWT required for settings update authorization.
Fetch current settings to verify update differences and provide the base record for update mutation.

scenario.draft: Test validation errors when updating service settings with invalid data (e.g., negative max_post_length, malformed field). After admin authentication, attempt to set fields out of allowed range or type. Verify that the endpoint responds with appropriate validation errors and that settings remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for elevated settings edit privilege.
Admin authentication for update operation.
Fetch the settings to perform an invalid update mutation and to assert no changes occurred after failed update.

scenario.draft: Test authorization error on settings update attempt with non-admin or unauthenticated user. Try updating global settings using either a basic member token or no authentication at all. Verify that the API securely denies the operation and returns an appropriate authorization error.

dependencies.purpose: Register as admin for a baseline valid use scenario.
Obtain valid admin JWT for comparison, then simulate invalid, member, or missing tokens for unauthorized test.

scenario.draft: Test successful search and retrieval of a paginated guest session record list using advanced filters as an authenticated admin. Register and log in as admin, then call the patch endpoint with various filter criteria (date range, consent status, device info) to ensure correct pagination, filtering, and result structure. All guest data, including IP and consent fields, should be returned as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to gain permission for guest session search.
Login as admin to obtain the JWT necessary for this endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test that search with filters that match no guest records returns an empty result set with proper pagination response. As admin, call the endpoint with a filter combination that does not correspond to any guest records and verify structure of the empty response.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin account for permissions context.
Login as admin to obtain access to the endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test that unauthorized or non-admin users cannot access the guest search endpoint. Attempt to call the search endpoint without authentication or with a basic member's JWT. Confirm the endpoint returns an authorization error and guest data remains protected.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user as the positive test case for contrast.
Produce valid admin tokens for direct use and manipulation in negative scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a guest session detail by ID as admin. Includes setup: register admin, login, retrieve a guest session using the search endpoint to get a valid guestId, then retrieve details using the get endpoint. Assert that all sensitive and metadata fields are returned for audit and admin review.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account to access guest details.
Authenticate and get JWT for admin-level authorization.
List guest session records to acquire a valid guestId for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test access denied and correct error on retrieving a guest session using an invalid or unauthorized admin token, or when guestId does not exist. This ensures access is secured and sensitive guest metadata is not leaked. Attempt with invalid meeting security and not-found error scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for permission context.
Obtain a valid JWT token for negative scenario manipulation.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of discussion board categories as an admin. Create an admin account and authenticate to obtain a valid session. Ensure categories are already created using the category creation endpoint. Request the category listing with various filtering parameters (by name, display order, and description), validating: (1) Success returns correct paginated results; (2) Results reflect up-to-date display order; (3) Filtering by partial match on name or description functions as expected; (4) Pagination metadata is correct; (5) All fields id, name, description, display_order, created_at, and updated_at are present and accurate.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin user to enable management operations on board categories.
Authenticate as admin to obtain session/JWT for subsequent API calls.
Create at least one category to ensure there are records available to search and filter. May be repeated to ensure multiple categories for pagination/filtering scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test that unauthorized users (non-admin roles) cannot access the admin category listing endpoint. Attempt to access the endpoint while authenticated as a member or moderator, and also with no authentication header. Verify the system returns descriptive errors for insufficient privilege or missing authentication. Business rules should prevent all non-admin access, ensuring security. Also, check that the error response is clear and actionable.

dependencies.purpose: Register as a regular member to attempt unauthorized access and validate permission enforcement.
Login as member and use member JWT to test permission denial.
Register as a moderator to test moderator-level access denial.
Login as moderator and use moderator JWT to test restricted permission scenario.

scenario.draft: Test listing categories when none are present or when filter parameters do not match any records. As an authenticated admin, call the search endpoint when the categories table is empty, and again with filter parameters (e.g., unique random strings) that yield no results. Confirm an empty list and correct pagination metadata are returned, demonstrating the system’s ability to gracefully handle zero-result edge cases.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to obtain authorized access.
Authenticate as admin for permission.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the full details of a specific category by ID as an admin. First, register and authenticate as admin, create a new board category, then retrieve it by its ID using this endpoint. Validate all fields (id, name, description, display_order, created_at, updated_at) are correctly returned and match the creation payload. Also, validate that the admin role can access any valid category, and the returned details reflect the most recent saved state.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to access category detail functions.
Authenticate as admin to obtain permissions.
Create a new category and retrieve its ID needed for detail lookup.

scenario.draft: Test error handling for requests involving a non-existent or invalid categoryId as an admin. Authenticate as admin, then attempt to fetch a category using (a) a random UUID not linked to any category, and (b) an incorrectly formatted ID (e.g., non-UUID or empty string). Assert responses return a suitable not found or validation error with a clear, descriptive message that aids in diagnosing incorrect usage or non-existent resources.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for access.
Authenticate as admin for permissions.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new category by an admin. Register and authenticate as an admin. Attempt to create a category with valid data (unique name 2–60 chars, optional description <=255 chars, integer display order), verifying: (a) returned object includes all necessary fields and generated UUID; (b) name uniqueness is enforced. Also validate that required fields trigger error responses when omitted or violating length/business constraints (test with too-short name, too-long name, absent name, excessively long description, and missing display order).

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for category management.
Login as admin to obtain authorization.

scenario.draft: Test error response when attempting to create a category with a name that already exists. Register and log in as admin. Create a category with a unique name, then submit a second category creation request with the exact same name. Verify the system rejects the request with a conflict error, confirming uniqueness enforcement. Error messaging should be clear about the duplication business rule violation.

dependencies.purpose: Register for admin permissions.
Login to acquire session.
Create the initial category whose name will be duplicated.

scenario.draft: Test successfully updating a category as an admin as well as handling uniqueness conflicts. Register and login as an admin user, create two categories, and then: (a) update the first category with new values for name, description, or display order—verify the updated values are reflected and timestamps are updated; (b) attempt to update the second category with a name that already exists (from the first category) to verify that uniqueness conflicts are properly caught and result in a descriptive error. Also test partial updates—changing only some of the fields—and confirm only those fields are altered.

dependencies.purpose: Register to initiate admin operations.
Authenticate for API permissions.
Create the first and second category, both required for uniqueness conflict scenario.

scenario.draft: Test updating a category using a non-existent or invalid category ID as an admin. Attempt to update a category by supplying a random UUID that does not correspond to any record and then an invalid (malformed) ID. Expect descriptive error responses: not found or validation errors with actionable messages to help correct usage.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for access.
Authenticate as admin for update operation.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion of a category by admin and handling referential integrity. Create and authenticate an admin, then create a standalone category (not referenced by any boards or posts). Delete the category and verify it is removed from listing and not retrievable. Next, attempt to delete a category that is referenced by an existing board or post (create category, create board linked to it); ensure deletion is blocked and error message clearly explains referential integrity prevention.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for category management.
Login to obtain admin session/token.
Create a new category to test simple deletion.
Create a board referencing a category in order to test referential integrity constraints on delete.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a category using an invalid or non-existent categoryId as admin. Attempt category deletion with a random UUID and then an invalid ID format. Validate that each results in a not found or validation error, verifying the business logic protects against deletion of non-existent resources and reports errors clearly.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin for access.
Login as admin for permission.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a moderator-board assignment's full details as an admin. Register an admin account and login to obtain a valid token. Create a new board and moderator account, then assign a moderator to the board using the admin privileges. After assignment creation, use the returned assignment ID to fetch the detail view. Assert all expected fields (including resolved references to moderator, board, assignment period, and admin reference) are included in the response. Validate compliance with role access restrictions and completeness of audit-relevant metadata returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register and obtain admin privileges for authorization prerequisite.
Login as admin to issue tokens for authenticated requests.
Create a board to be assigned for moderator responsibility.
Register a moderator account to use for assignment.
Assign the moderator to the created board and retrieve the unique assignment ID for testing detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test the error response when attempting to fetch details of a non-existent moderator-board assignment as an admin. Register and login as admin. Attempt a GET with a randomly generated or invalid UUID for moderatorBoardAssignmentId that does not correspond to any record. Confirm that the API returns an appropriate not-found or error message according to business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for permissioned API access.
Login as admin to authorize the error scenario request.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a valid moderator-board assignment by an admin. This includes the scenario where a board and a moderator both exist and the assignment maps responsibility with correct timing and optional admin log/rationale. Register and login as admin, create a board, and register a moderator. Then, as admin, create a board assignment linking the moderator to the newly created board. Assert the response contains the correctly assigned moderator, board, admin info, assignment period, and audit fields.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to carry out privileged actions.
Login as the admin to obtain authentication.
Create a new board to serve as the moderation target for assignment.
Register a new moderator account to be assigned.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a moderator-board assignment with duplicate assignment constraints. Register as admin, login, create a board, and register a moderator. Assign the moderator to the board successfully. Then, attempt to assign the same moderator to the same board again and verify the system rejects the duplicate with a proper conflict or business logic error message.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for assignment creation and testing duplicate logic.
Login as admin, required for assignment actions.
Create a board for moderator assignment.
Create moderator account to be used for the assignments.
Create initial valid assignment establishing a duplicate condition for the next request.

scenario.draft: Test admin update of moderator-board assignment record, such as closing an assignment (setting an end date) or updating the assignment log metadata. Register, login, create both a board and moderator, then assign the moderator to the board as admin. Next, perform an update on the assignment by ID, modifying permitted fields (e.g., ending the assignment, modifying notes, updating operational admin reference). Verify results include updated fields and that audit compliance (modification logs) are satisfied.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for privileged access.
Login as the admin to get authentication token.
Create a board for moderator to be assigned to.
Create moderator to be assigned.
Assign moderator to board and retrieve assignment for update.

scenario.draft: Test update scenario where moderator-board assignment does not exist. Register and login as admin. Attempt an update with a random or invalid UUID for moderatorBoardAssignmentId. Confirm a not-found or appropriate error response is received.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for authorized test execution.
Admin login for authentication context.

Register and login as admin, create board and moderator, successfully assign moderator to the board, then delete the assignment. The response must match the search criteria exactly, and the test should also cover edge cases such as empty results and invalid filters.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account to gain access to the admin search API.
Login the admin to acquire valid authentication tokens for API usage.
Create multiple posts under different categories, authored by different members, to populate test data for various search scenarios.
Create additional posts with varied titles and contents, including keywords to test filtering and search accuracy.

scenario.draft: Validate that a logged-in member can successfully retrieve the full detail of an accessible post by its unique postId, including title, body, authorship, status, and business metadata. Ensure permission boundaries: authors can retrieve their own posts regardless of flag state, while members may only access public, active posts. Include cases for posts that are deleted or flagged, and verify that appropriate errors or status codes are returned for posts the member should not access (e.g., private or removed posts).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to enable authenticated post access.
Login as the member to obtain a valid session token for requests.
Create a new post as the member to use for detail retrieval testing.
Modify the post state (e.g., soft-delete or flag) to test edge-case access and permission enforcement.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of a comment by its author within the allowed edit window, validating updated body text and returned metadata. Confirm edit fails if attempted after the window closes. Attempt to update a comment authored by another member and expect a permission denial. Cover cases such as updating a deleted, flagged, or locked comment and expect the operation to be rejected with appropriate error messages.

dependencies.purpose: Register two member accounts: one as the comment author, and a second for permission edge-case testing.
Login as the comment author for normal update scenarios and as the second member for permission-denial scenarios.
Create a post for comment actions.
Create comments by both members for edit and permission tests.
Soft-delete a comment to test updates on removed or locked comments.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a moderator can update (edit) any comment regardless of authorship and edit window constraints, reflecting moderation privileges. This includes updating comments that are flagged, deleted, locked, or otherwise restricted to normal members. Test for failure cases such as attempting to edit a comment on a post that does not exist, a comment ID that is wrong, or when the moderator's account is no longer active. Validate that audit trails are updated and all business rule restrictions are respected.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator account to test moderator privileges.
Perform moderator login to obtain JWT for privileged operations.
Create member posts for comment test coverage.
Create comments as regular members, which the moderator will attempt to update.
Soft-delete comments to validate moderator override permissions.

scenario.draft: Test successful deletion (soft-delete) of a specific comment edit record as an admin. The scenario begins with admin registration and login to set up authentication. A member creates a post and a comment, and then edits the comment to generate at least one comment edit history item. The admin then navigates to delete a specific comment edit record using a valid commentEditId. Validate that the edit record is marked deleted (deleted_at is set) and inaccessible via normal member or moderation flows, but remains in admin/audit trails as per policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin (creates account and provides credentials for privileged operations).
Login as admin to obtain the necessary authorization token for further requests.
Register a member who will create the original comment.
Login as member to create post and comment.
Create a post as the test member, to allow comment creation and editing.
Create the original comment which will be edited.
Edit the comment, generating a comment edit history record.

scenario.draft: Test error scenario: attempt to delete a comment edit record by an admin where the specified commentEditId does not exist. Admin authentication is established as per business policy. The scenario proceeds to call the delete endpoint with a random or invalid commentEditId value (not matching any existing record for the referenced comment/post). Assert that the system returns a not found error or appropriate message, does not affect any valid records, and provides actionable feedback for the admin.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for privilege acquisition.
Login as admin for authorization context.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of paginated and filterable votes for a specific post as a member. After registering and logging in as a member, a post is created. The member and at least one additional member cast votes on the post. The scenario calls the PATCH votes endpoint for the post, applying filters such as vote value (upvote/downvote), voter_member_id, and date range. The API should return paginated vote results matching the filter criteria, along with analytics metadata (total upvotes/downvotes).

dependencies.purpose: Register initial member.
Login as initial member.
Create a post on which votes will be cast.
Cast a vote as initial member.
Register a second member for diverse voting data.
Login as second member.
Second member casts a vote on the same post.

scenario.draft: Test the vote search endpoint for a post that has no votes. After member registration and post creation, no votes are cast. The member requests the vote list via the PATCH endpoint. The response should return an empty vote list, confirm correct pagination structure, and indicate zero vote counts.

dependencies.purpose: Register member for test context.
Login as member to receive authorization.
Post creation by member; no votes are cast after this.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can search and access all votes cast on a post, including those by other members. Register and login as a moderator, then create a post (via member), have several members cast votes. The moderator uses the PATCH endpoint to retrieve votes for the post, filters by different parameters (voter ID, value), and verifies full visibility as permitted for moderation role.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator enabling privileged access.
Login as moderator for authorization.
Register a member to create a post and initial votes.
Login as member for post creation and voting.
Member creates a post.
First member votes on post.
Register a second member for additional votes.
Login as second member.
Second member casts a vote on the post.

scenario.draft: Test error handling for searching votes on a non-existent post as a moderator. Moderator is authenticated and attempts to fetch votes for a random invalid postId. The API returns a not found error or equivalent, with no data leak, and an appropriate business error message for moderation dashboards.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator.
Login as moderator for roles/context.

scenario.draft: Test error condition: moderator attempts to delete an attachment using an invalid or non-existent attachmentId for a given post. The API should return a not found or business error, leave existing attachments unchanged, and provide an actionable message for compliance tracking.

dependencies.purpose: Moderator registration.
Moderator login for permission context.

scenario.draft: Test successful removal of a post attachment by an admin. Admin registers and logs in, sets up a member who creates a post and uploads an attachment. Admin executes the DELETE on the attachmentId. The attachment must be marked deleted (soft/hard depending on policy), disappear from standard listing, and the operation is logged in system audit. Access to the file after deletion must be denied or result in an error per compliance rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for privileged access.
Login as admin.
Register member for post/attachment context.
Member login.
Member creates a post.
Member attaches a file to the post.

scenario.draft: Test error: admin attempts to delete an attachment already marked deleted or which does not exist. Admin is authenticated, attempts DELETE on an invalid or previously-deleted attachmentId. API returns a relevant business error; audit verifies action and no resource change occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin.
Login as admin.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of a comment by an admin user. Begin by registering a new member and creating a post. Have the member add a comment to the post. Register and login as an admin user, then perform a PUT request to update the comment's content and verify that the response reflects the changes. This scenario ensures that admins can update any comment regardless of original authorship and that audit records show the edit.

Login to acquire admin authentication for performing privilege operations.
Create a post as the registered member; needed as parent entity for the comment.
Create a comment on the post, as the member, to set up a target for admin update.

scenario.draft: Test that a non-admin user cannot update a comment via the admin endpoint. Register as a member and create a post and comment. Without admin authentication, attempt to update the comment via the admin endpoint and expect a permission denied or forbidden error, validating that role-based restrictions are correctly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register a standard member account for comment creation and attempted unauthorized update.

Create a post as the member for comment association.
Add a comment as the member, which will be the target for the forbidden update attempt.

scenario.draft: Validate that a member can successfully delete their own comment within the allowed business window. Register a member, create a post, add a comment, and then, as the author, perform a deletion. Confirm that the comment is soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), and that it is hidden from subsequent standard list queries but visible in audit/moderation views if tested further.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member who will create the post and comment.
Authenticate as the member for all subsequent operations.
Create a post belonging to the member, required for comment creation.
Create a comment on the post as the member, which will then be deleted.

scenario.draft: Verify deletion is not allowed after the edit/delete window expires according to business rules. Register and login as a member, create a post and comment, wait or simulate the expiry of the delete window, then attempt to delete the comment. Expect a forbidden or business error indicating the delete operation is not allowed.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to generate a comment deletion edge case.
Login as this member for session/auth establishment.
Create a post for associating the comment.
Create a comment to be the target for post-window delete attempt.

scenario.draft: Test successful soft deletion of a comment by a moderator. Register a member and a moderator, create a post and a comment by the member, then have the moderator delete the comment. The system should mark the comment as deleted (deleted_at set), the comment should disappear from standard listings, and the deletion should appear in audit/moderation logs.

Member creates a post as the target for a comment.
Member creates a comment that the moderator will delete.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a non-existent comment by a moderator returns a suitable error. After registering and logging in as a moderator, attempt to delete a comment using an invalid or random UUID not present in the database. Expect a not found error, confirming the system's correct error handling for missing resources.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for privileged operations.
Login as the moderator to get proper permissions.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can update mutable fields on a comment edit record, such as the edit reason or audit note. Register a member and an admin, create a post and comment, create a comment edit, then update the comment edit as admin providing new rationale or metadata. Verify the changes are reflected and fully audit-trailed.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update an immutable or forbidden field (such as editId or non-mutable audit fields) in a comment edit as an admin. The API should reject this change and respond with an error, ensuring that only permitted fields may be edited per compliance rules.

Register a member and a moderator, create a post, comment, and comment edit record, then delete the comment edit as the moderator. Verify the edit is marked as deleted (deleted_at set), and that it is no longer listed in standard revision history queries but available for audit if business logic provides.

Member adds a comment.
